<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span><span id="A1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>: Probe Based learning using Hidden Neural Activations</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this appendix we describe in full detail <span id="A1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>, our probe-based architecture for learning from hidden-layer activations.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span><span id="A1.SS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>: A probe-based model for learning on weight spaces</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We begin by discussing the permutation symmetries of hidden activations induced by weight-space symmetries, which motivate the design of <span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Symmetries in weight spaces and hidden Layers</h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Consider a depth-<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> MLP. Let <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{0}=P_{L}=I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{0}=P_{L}=I</annotation></semantics></math>, and let
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{1},\ldots,P_{L-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{1},\ldots,P_{L-1}</annotation></semantics></math> be arbitrary permutation matrices. The transformation</p>
<table id="A1.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textstyle W_{i}\mapsto P_{i+1}W_{i}P_{i}^{\top},\,b_{i}\mapsto P_{i+1}b_{i},\,0\leq i&lt;L," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textstyle W_{i}\mapsto P_{i+1}W_{i}P_{i}^{\top},\,b_{i}\mapsto P_{i+1}b_{i},\,0\leq i&lt;L,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">permutes the neurons within the hidden layers while leaving the realized function unchanged. As shown in prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Navon et al. (2023)</a></cite>, architectures that explicitly respect these symmetries can substantially outperform models that ignore them. We therefore design <span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> to be invariant to hidden-neuron permutations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under the above transformation, the representation at hidden layer <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> transforms as <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}(p;\theta)\mapsto P_{i}x_{i}(p;\theta),\,i\in[L-1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}(p;\theta)\mapsto P_{i}x_{i}(p;\theta),\,i\in[L-1]</annotation></semantics></math>
Thus, each hidden layer is equivariant to its corresponding permutation <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In contrast, the input and final output are unchanged, since <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{0}=P_{L}=I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{0}=P_{L}=I</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We now describe how this symmetry acts on hidden probe responses. Consider a tuple of probes <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N}).</annotation></semantics></math> For hidden layer <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, define the response vector of neuron <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> across all probes as
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{i,k}\coloneqq\left(x_{i,k}(p_{1};\theta),\ldots,x_{i,k}(p_{N};\theta)\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{N}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{i,k}\coloneqq\left(x_{i,k}(p_{1};\theta),\ldots,x_{i,k}(p_{N};\theta)\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{N}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Since <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is equivariant to <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, applying a hidden-neuron permutation simply permutes the collection <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\{v^{i,k}:k\in[d_{i}]\right\}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\{v^{i,k}:k\in[d_{i}]\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Therefore, each hidden layer is naturally represented as an unordered set of
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> vectors in <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>N</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Overview of <span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> </h5>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Motivated by this observation, <span id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> processes each hidden layer using a permutation-invariant set encoder. Specifically, we encode every hidden layer <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\phi}^{i}\coloneqq T_{\phi}^{i}\left(\left\{v^{i,k}:k\in[d_{i}]\right\}\right)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\phi}^{i}\coloneqq T_{\phi}^{i}\left(\left\{v^{i,k}:k\in[d_{i}]\right\}\right),</annotation></semantics></math>
where <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\phi}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\phi}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a layer-wise set encoder. In our implementation, <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\phi}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\phi}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is an invariant Set Transformer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. (2019)</a></cite>, making <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\phi}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\phi}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> invariant to permutations of the neurons in layer <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The resulting hidden-layer representations are concatenated in layer order,
together with the final-layer probe outputs:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textstyle\Phi_{\mathcal{P},\phi}^{\mathrm{hidden}}(\theta)=\left[r_{\phi}^{1};\ldots;r_{\phi}^{L-1};f(p_{1};\theta);\ldots;f(p_{N};\theta)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mi>hidden</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>;</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>;</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>;</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textstyle\Phi_{\mathcal{P},\phi}^{\mathrm{hidden}}(\theta)=\left[r_{\phi}^{1};\ldots;r_{\phi}^{L-1};f(p_{1};\theta);\ldots;f(p_{N};\theta)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A final predictor <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> maps this representation to the target: <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{y}(\theta)=\rho_{\phi}(\Phi_{\mathcal{P},\phi}^{\mathrm{hidden}}(\theta))." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mi>hidden</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{y}(\theta)=\rho_{\phi}(\Phi_{\mathcal{P},\phi}^{\mathrm{hidden}}(\theta)).</annotation></semantics></math> The probes <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},\ldots,p_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},\ldots,p_{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, the layer-wise encoders
<math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\phi}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>ϕ</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\phi}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> (allowed to be different across layers but can have shared parameters to reduce overall parameter count), and the predictor <math id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> are trained jointly.
The learned probes are shared across all target networks.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span><span id="A1.SS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> for transformers</h3>

<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Learning a mixed-length probe bank.</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Here we introduce <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>, a probe-based model for learning on softmax-attention based transformers. Our reconstruction arguments from Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 5 (Structured probing for softmax attention). ‣ 4 Identifying Multi-Head Attention from Probes ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> and Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ B.4 Function-level identification of multi-head attention ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> use different sequence lengths: singleton probes recover the value matrix, while multi-token probes recover the attention weights. This suggests that probes of different lengths can provide complementary information about a target.
We retain this design principle, but learn a shared set of probes of varying sequence length rather than imposing the exact configurations.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Design of <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> predictor</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each probe <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{j}\in\mathcal{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{j}\in\mathcal{P}</annotation></semantics></math>, we record the outputs of the transformer
blocks, the final normalized token states, and the decoder output:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{T}_{\theta}=\left(X_{1}(P_{j};\theta),\cdots,X_{L}(P_{j};\theta),\,X_{\mathrm{norm}}(P_{j};\theta),\,f(P_{j};\theta)\right)_{P_{j}\in\mathcal{P}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>norm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{T}_{\theta}=\left(X_{1}(P_{j};\theta),\cdots,X_{L}(P_{j};\theta),\,X_{\mathrm{norm}}(P_{j};\theta),\,f(P_{j};\theta)\right)_{P_{j}\in\mathcal{P}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">For each observed layer and channel, we concatenate its
responses across all probes and token positions, using a fixed
order. A shared MLP encodes each resulting channel trajectory
into one feature vector.
These channel features and final logit features are passed to a transformer followed by an MLP to give the output: <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{y}_{\theta}=R_{\phi}(\mathcal{T}_{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{y}_{\theta}=R_{\phi}(\mathcal{T}_{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Incorporating weight space symmetries</h5>

<div id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Head permutations and the transformations
<math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{a}\mapsto Q_{a}R_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{a}\mapsto Q_{a}R_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{a}\mapsto K_{a}R_{a}^{-\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mo lspace="0em">⁣</mo><mo>⊤</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{a}\mapsto K_{a}R_{a}^{-\top}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{a}\mapsto V_{a}S_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{a}\mapsto V_{a}S_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{a}\mapsto S_{a}^{-1}O_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O_{a}\mapsto S_{a}^{-1}O_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>,
for invertible <math id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{a},S_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{a},S_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>, leave the attention output
unchanged. Consequently, they leave every recorded block
response and classifier output unchanged, so <span id="A1.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> is invariant to these symmetries by design. Handling such symmetries remains a key challenge in works like <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tran et al. (2025)</a></cite>, which we get for free.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Proof of Technical results</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">See <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Unique reconstruction from finite samples). ‣ 2 Identifying Analytic Neural Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof is based on the Finite Witness Theorem (Theorem A.2 in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amir et al. (2023)</a></cite>), which states that, for an analytic <math id="A2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G:\mathbb{R}^{a}\times\mathbb{R}^{b}\to\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>a</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>b</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G:\mathbb{R}^{a}\times\mathbb{R}^{b}\to\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, and Lebesgue almost every <math id="A2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1},\ldots,w_{a+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>b</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1},\ldots,w_{a+1}\in\mathbb{R}^{b}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{a}|\,G(y;w_{i})=0,\forall i=1,\ldots,a+1\}=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{a}|\,G(y;w)=0,\forall w\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>a</mi></msup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>a</mi></msup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>G</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>w</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>b</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{a}|\,G(y;w_{i})=0,\forall i=1,\ldots,a+1\}=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{a}|\,G(y;w)=0,\forall w\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">To prove our theorem, we define the real analytic function <math id="A2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(\theta_{1},\theta_{2};p):=\|f(p;\theta_{1})-f(p;\theta_{2})\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(\theta_{1},\theta_{2};p):=\|f(p;\theta_{1})-f(p;\theta_{2})\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since the pair <math id="A2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\theta_{1},\theta_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\theta_{1},\theta_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> resides in <math id="A2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{2q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{2q}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Finite Witness Theorem implies that for <math id="A2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q+1</annotation></semantics></math> random samples <math id="A2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},\ldots,p_{2q+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},\ldots,p_{2q+1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we will have that for all <math id="A2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{1},\theta_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{1},\theta_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(p_{i};\theta_{1})-f(p_{i};\theta_{2})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(p_{i};\theta_{1})-f(p_{i};\theta_{2})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,\ldots,2q+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,\ldots,2q+1</annotation></semantics></math>, if and only if <math id="A2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(p;\theta_{1})-f(p;\theta_{2})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(p;\theta_{1})-f(p;\theta_{2})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Identification of Analytic MLPs from Hidden Probes</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We borrow notations from Section <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Hidden probes provide useful information: ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> and Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title='Algorithm 1 ‣ Algorithm to recover weights from Ψ_"all" for generic targets ‣ B.1 Identification of Analytic MLPs from Hidden Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning' class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, but occasionally them slightly. Let <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\in\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\in\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{0},\ldots,d_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{0},\ldots,d_{L}</annotation></semantics></math> be positive
integers. Let <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> be nonempty, open, and connected.
For each <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,\ldots,L\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,\ldots,L\}</annotation></semantics></math>, let
<math id="A2.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{i}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{i}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> be nonempty, open, and connected,
and let <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{i}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{i-1}}\times\Theta_{i}\to\mathbb{R}^{d_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{i}:\mathbb{R}^{d_{i-1}}\times\Theta_{i}\to\mathbb{R}^{d_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>
be jointly real analytic. Define the following notations:</p>

<p id="A2.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Given a tuple of probes <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N})\in\mathcal{X}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N})\in\mathcal{X}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, define</p>

\mathbf{1}_{N}^{\top}\end{pmatrix}\end{split}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mtable columnspacing="0pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable displaystyle="true"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>x</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mi>x</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0.507em">,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msubsup><mn>𝟏</mn><mi>N</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{split}&amp;\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})\coloneqq\begin{pmatrix}x_{i}(p_{1};\theta)\cdots x_{i}(p_{N};\theta)\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{i}\times N},\,i=0,\ldots,L.\\
&amp;\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}\\
\mathbf{1}_{N}^{\top}\end{pmatrix}\end{split}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Thus, full intermediate observation records the sampled
states at every layer, including the final output.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Identification of Arbitrary Analytic Nets from Hidden Layers:</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Unique reconstruction from finite samples). ‣ 2 Identifying Analytic Neural Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> shows that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q+1</annotation></semantics></math> final-layer probes suffice to distinguish any two functionally distinct models in an analytic family. Here, we show that for analytic sequential models of the form in (<a href="#A2.E4" title="In B.1 Identification of Analytic MLPs from Hidden Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), access to intermediate-layer observations reduces the sufficient probe count to <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q+q_{\max}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q+q_{\max}+1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 8</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Identification from intermediate observations)<span id="Thmtheorem8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmtheorem8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Under the preceding assumptions, suppose
<math id="Thmtheorem8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq q+q_{\max}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq q+q_{\max}+1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, for Lebesgue-almost every <math id="Thmtheorem8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{X}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{X}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>,
simultaneously for every <math id="Thmtheorem8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta,\theta^{\prime}\in\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta,\theta^{\prime}\in\Theta</annotation></semantics></math>, one has</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in[L]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in[L]</annotation></semantics></math>, we use the following notations:</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1</annotation></semantics></math>, set <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{&lt;1}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{&lt;1}=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{&lt;1}=\mathbb{R}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>0</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{&lt;1}=\mathbb{R}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The state <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i-1}(u;\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i-1}(u;\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> depends only on

For <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=(\eta_{1},\cdots,\eta_{i-1})\in\Theta_{&lt;i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=(\eta_{1},\cdots,\eta_{i-1})\in\Theta_{&lt;i}</annotation></semantics></math>,
we therefore write <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i-1}(u;\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i-1}(u;\eta)</annotation></semantics></math> for the state
generated by these blocks and for <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1</annotation></semantics></math>, this means

</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">We define <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{i}\coloneqq\Theta_{&lt;i}\times\Theta_{i}\times\Theta_{i}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{i}\coloneqq\Theta_{&lt;i}\times\Theta_{i}\times\Theta_{i},</annotation></semantics></math>

By composition, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is jointly real analytic on
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}\times\Omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}\times\Omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is an open connected
subset of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{Q_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{Q_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover, we have</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex15"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle Q_{i}+1=q_{&lt;i}+2q_{i}+1\leq q+q_{i}+1\leq q+q_{\max}+1\leq N." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle Q_{i}+1=q_{&lt;i}+2q_{i}+1\leq q+q_{i}+1\leq q+q_{\max}+1\leq N.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">The Finite Witness Theorem
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amir et al., 2023</a>, Theorem A.2)</cite>
provides a Lebesgue-null set
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{i}\subseteq\mathcal{X}^{Q_{i}+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{i}\subseteq\mathcal{X}^{Q_{i}+1}</annotation></semantics></math> such that, for every
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p_{1},\cdots,p_{Q_{i}+1})\notin E_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(p_{1},\cdots,p_{Q_{i}+1})\notin E_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and every
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\eta,\alpha,\beta)\in\Omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\eta,\alpha,\beta)\in\Omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex16"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle H_{i}(p_{n};\eta,\alpha,\beta)=0,\ \forall\,n\in[Q_{i}+1]\implies H_{i}(u;\eta,\alpha,\beta)=0,\ \forall\,u\in\mathcal{X}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle H_{i}(p_{n};\eta,\alpha,\beta)=0,\ \forall\,n\in[Q_{i}+1]\implies H_{i}(u;\eta,\alpha,\beta)=0,\ \forall\,u\in\mathcal{X}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">We define <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}\coloneqq E_{i}\times\mathcal{X}^{N-Q_{i}-1},\,B\coloneqq\bigcup_{i=1}^{L}B_{i}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">≔</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}\coloneqq E_{i}\times\mathcal{X}^{N-Q_{i}-1},\,B\coloneqq\bigcup_{i=1}^{L}B_{i},</annotation></semantics></math>
where <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a singleton.
Each <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, and hence <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, is Lebesgue-null.
For every <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\cdots,p_{N})\notin B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∉</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\cdots,p_{N})\notin B</annotation></semantics></math>, the preceding
implication holds at every layer, simultaneously for
all <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\eta,\alpha,\beta)\in\Omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\eta,\alpha,\beta)\in\Omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In particular, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on the pair of
parameters being compared.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\notin B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∉</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\notin B</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=(\theta_{1},\cdots,\theta_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=(\theta_{1},\cdots,\theta_{L})</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{\prime}=(\theta_{1}^{\prime},\cdots,\theta_{L}^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{\prime}=(\theta_{1}^{\prime},\cdots,\theta_{L}^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta^{\prime}}(\mathcal{P}),\,i=0,\cdots,L." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>i</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta^{\prime}}(\mathcal{P}),\,i=0,\cdots,L.</annotation></semantics></math>
We prove by induction that
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}(\cdot;\theta)\equiv x_{i}(\cdot;\theta^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}(\cdot;\theta)\equiv x_{i}(\cdot;\theta^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=0</annotation></semantics></math>, both maps are the identity.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Suppose the assertion holds for <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i-1</annotation></semantics></math>, and set
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=(\theta_{1},\cdots,\theta_{i-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=(\theta_{1},\cdots,\theta_{i-1})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, for every <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle x_{i-1}(u;\eta)=x_{i-1}(u;\theta)=x_{i-1}(u;\theta^{\prime}),\,\text{and}\,H_{i}(u;\eta,\theta_{i},\theta_{i}^{\prime})=\left\|x_{i}(u;\theta)-x_{i}(u;\theta^{\prime})\right\|_{2}^{2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>and</mtext><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle x_{i-1}(u;\eta)=x_{i-1}(u;\theta)=x_{i-1}(u;\theta^{\prime}),\,\text{and}\,H_{i}(u;\eta,\theta_{i},\theta_{i}^{\prime})=\left\|x_{i}(u;\theta)-x_{i}(u;\theta^{\prime})\right\|_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Equality at the probes <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}</annotation></semantics></math> therefore gives
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H_{i}(p_{n};\eta,\theta_{i},\theta_{i}^{\prime})=0,\,n=1,\cdots,N." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}(p_{n};\eta,\theta_{i},\theta_{i}^{\prime})=0,\,n=1,\cdots,N.</annotation></semantics></math>
Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\notin B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\notin B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the finite witness theorem
implies
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{i}(u;\eta,\theta_{i},\theta_{i}^{\prime})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{i}(u;\eta,\theta_{i},\theta_{i}^{\prime})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}(\cdot;\theta)\equiv x_{i}(\cdot;\theta^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≡</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}(\cdot;\theta)\equiv x_{i}(\cdot;\theta^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>,
completing the induction.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">When the activation is also injective and non polynomial:</h5>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now show that if the activation is analytic, injective, and non-polynomial, the sufficient number of probes can be substantially reduced. We prove a stronger version of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Reconstruction from hidden layer activations). ‣ 3.1 Hidden probes provide useful information: ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> for that. We first prove a couple of lemmas that will be useful in proving the result.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We consider the non-trivial case <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Choose <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\in\mathbb{R}^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\in\mathbb{R}^{q}</annotation></semantics></math> such that the numbers <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{n}\coloneqq v^{\top}y_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{n}\coloneqq v^{\top}y_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in[K]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in[K]</annotation></semantics></math>, are pairwise distinct. Such a choice is possible because the
bad set is the finite union of proper hyperplanes
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigcup_{n&lt;n^{\prime}}\{v\in\mathbb{R}^{q}:v^{\top}(y_{n}-y_{n^{\prime}})=0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigcup_{n&lt;n^{\prime}}\{v\in\mathbb{R}^{q}:v^{\top}(y_{n}-y_{n^{\prime}})=0\}</annotation></semantics></math>, each of which is
proper since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{n}\neq y_{n^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{n}\neq y_{n^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We first prove the span claim. Suppose, for contradiction, that the
span is proper. Then there exists a nonzero vector
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=(c_{1},\ldots,c_{K})\in\mathbb{R}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>K</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=(c_{1},\ldots,c_{K})\in\mathbb{R}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math> such that</span></p>
<table id="A2.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{split}&amp;\sum_{n=1}^{K}c_{n}\sigma(w^{\top}y_{n}+b)=0\,\forall\,(w,b)\in\mathbb{R}^{q}\times\mathbb{R}\\

\implies&amp;\sum_{n=1}^{K}c_{n}\sigma(b+at_{n})=0\,\forall\,a,b\in\mathbb{R},\,\text{by taking }w=av.\end{split}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is real analytic and non-polynomial, none of the
derivatives <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=0,\ldots,K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=0,\ldots,K-1</annotation></semantics></math>, is identically zero.
Indeed, if <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{(k)}\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{(k)}\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> would be a
polynomial of degree at most <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k-1</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, for each
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=0,\ldots,K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=0,\ldots,K-1</annotation></semantics></math>, the zero set of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math> is a proper discrete
subset of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℝ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence the finite union
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bigcup_{k=0}^{K-1}\{b\in\mathbb{R}:\sigma^{(k)}(b)=0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bigcup_{k=0}^{K-1}\{b\in\mathbb{R}:\sigma^{(k)}(b)=0\}</annotation></semantics></math> does not cover <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℝ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Choose <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{0}\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{0}\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> outside this union. Then we have:</span></p>
