<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.7.1" class="ltx_text">We first show that there exists some <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(K-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(K-1)</annotation></semantics></math>-tuple of parameters such
that the matrix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is full rank. We start with the one-dimensional
subspace <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{0}\coloneqq\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf{1}_{K}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mi>span</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{0}\coloneqq\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf{1}_{K}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. If every
vector <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v(w,b)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(w,b)</annotation></semantics></math> belonged to <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, then the span of all ridge vectors
would be contained in <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, but these vectors span <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>K</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>. exists <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{1},b_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{1},b_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m42" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v(w_{1},b_{1})\notin V_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(w_{1},b_{1})\notin V_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. Set
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m43" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{1}\coloneqq\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf{1}_{K},v(w_{1},b_{1})\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mi>span</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{1}\coloneqq\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf{1}_{K},v(w_{1},b_{1})\}</annotation></semantics></math>. inductively (as long as <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m44" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim V_{j}&lt;K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim V_{j}&lt;K</annotation></semantics></math> some ridge vector lies outside
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m45" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>), after <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m46" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K-1</annotation></semantics></math> steps we obtain parameters
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m47" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{1},b_{1}),\ldots,(w_{K-1},b_{K-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{1},b_{1}),\ldots,(w_{K-1},b_{K-1})</annotation></semantics></math> such that the <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m48" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> vectors</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.8.1" class="ltx_text">are linearly independent in <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m49" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>K</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since there are <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m50" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> such vectors,
they form a basis of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m51" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>K</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math>. Equivalently, the corresponding matrix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m52" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>
has nonzero determinant for at least one choice of parameters.
Now we define</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.9.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m53" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is real analytic, every entry of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m54" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is a real-analytic
function of the parameters <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m55" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{1},b_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{1},b_{1})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m56" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ldots" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ldots</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m57" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{K-1},b_{K-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{K-1},b_{K-1})</annotation></semantics></math>,
and therefore <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m58" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is real analytic on the connected open set
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m59" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbb{R}^{q}\times\mathbb{R})^{K-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>q</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbb{R}^{q}\times\mathbb{R})^{K-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. The preceding construction shows that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m60" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>
is not identically zero. Hence its zero set is the zero set of a
nonzero real-analytic function on a connected open set, so it has
Hausdorff dimension strictly smaller than <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m61" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(K-1)(q+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(K-1)(q+1)</annotation></semantics></math>, implying zero
Lebesgue measure. Therefore <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.m62" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible for Lebesgue-a.e. choice
of the ridge parameters.
∎</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Now, for the following lemma, we define another notation for MLPs with width sequence <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}\coloneqq(d=d_{0},d_{1},\cdots,d_{L-1},d_{L}=m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}\coloneqq(d=d_{0},d_{1},\cdots,d_{L-1},d_{L}=m)</annotation></semantics></math>. For probes <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{X}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{X}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\in\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\in\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we recall the definitions <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})\coloneqq\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})\\
\mathbf{1}_{N}^{\top}\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb{R}^{(d_{i}+1)\times N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msubsup><mn>𝟏</mn><mi>N</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})\coloneqq\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})\\

We show that, for sufficiently large <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\coloneqq|\mathcal{P}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\coloneqq|\mathcal{P}|</annotation></semantics></math>, the matrix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> is almost always full rank.</p>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> has nonempty interior, choose <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B(x_{0},\epsilon)\subseteq\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B(x_{0},\epsilon)\subseteq\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{1},\ldots,e_{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{1},\ldots,e_{d}</annotation></semantics></math> be
the standard basis of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then the determinant</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx18" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">is nonzero for the choice of points
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{x_{0},x_{0}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}e_{1},\cdots,x_{0}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}e_{d}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{x_{0},x_{0}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}e_{1},\cdots,x_{0}+\frac{\epsilon}{2}e_{d}\}</annotation></semantics></math>:
subtracting the first column from each of the others gives the value
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm(\epsilon/2)^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm(\epsilon/2)^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> is not the zero polynomial. If a
probe tuple belongs to <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, then every <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d+1)\times(d+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d+1)\times(d+1)</annotation></semantics></math> minor of the
matrix in the definition of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes, so
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(p_{1},\ldots,p_{d+1})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(p_{1},\ldots,p_{d+1})=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m14" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="E_{1}\subseteq\{P=0\}\times\mathcal{X}^{N-d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{1}\subseteq\{P=0\}\times\mathcal{X}^{N-d-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> is a nonzero polynomial, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m16" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{P=0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{P=0\}</annotation></semantics></math> has Hausdorff dimension
strictly smaller than <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d+1)d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d+1)d</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}(E_{1})&lt;Nd" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}(E_{1})&lt;Nd</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, each diagonal set <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m19" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{p_{n}=p_{n^{\prime}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{p_{n}=p_{n^{\prime}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> has Hausdorff dimension
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N-1)d&lt;Nd" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N-1)d&lt;Nd</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> is a finite union of such sets, we have
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}(E)&lt;Nd" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}(E)&lt;Nd</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix a probe tuple <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N})\in\mathcal{X}^{N}\setminus E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>N</mi></msup><mo>∖</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N})\in\mathcal{X}^{N}\setminus E</annotation></semantics></math>. Then the
probes are pairwise distinct and
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{rank}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{0}(\mathcal{P})=d+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>rank</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{rank}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{0}(\mathcal{P})=d+1</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> and the sampled states
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}(p_{n};\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}(p_{n};\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> depend on <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=(B_{0},\ldots,B_{L-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=(B_{0},\ldots,B_{L-1})</annotation></semantics></math> only through
the blocks <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. We shall prove inductively that, for
Lebesgue-a.e. choice of the blocks <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, the following
two properties hold:</span></p>

<tbody id="A2.Ex33"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.4.1" class="ltx_text">Up to moving the row of ones to the bottom, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{i+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{i+1}</annotation></semantics></math> consists of the

is a <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d_{i+1}+1)\times(d_{i+1}+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d_{i+1}+1)\times(d_{i+1}+1)</annotation></semantics></math> minor of

Applying
Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma1" title="Lemma 1. ‣ When the activation is also injective and non polynomial: ‣ B.1 Identification of Analytic MLPs from Hidden Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> in <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> to the <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> points
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{1},\ldots,y_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1},\ldots,y_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> gives that, for Lebesgue-a.e. choice of the rows
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{1}^{\top},b_{1}),\ldots,(w_{d_{i+1}}^{\top},b_{d_{i+1}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>w</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{1}^{\top},b_{1}),\ldots,(w_{d_{i+1}}^{\top},b_{d_{i+1}})</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, the

Therefore, for Lebesgue-a.e. block
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{rank}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i+1}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=d_{i+1}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>rank</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{rank}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i+1}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=d_{i+1}+1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R_{i+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R_{i+1})</annotation></semantics></math> holds for Lebesgue-a.e. block <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, conditional on the
previous blocks satisfying <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m42" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>.
We next prove <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m43" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i+1})</annotation></semantics></math>. Fix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m44" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\neq n^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≠</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\neq n^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m45" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{n}\neq y_{n^{\prime}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{n}\neq y_{n^{\prime}}</annotation></semantics></math>, if
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m46" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i+1}(p_{n};\theta)=x_{i+1}(p_{n^{\prime}};\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i+1}(p_{n};\theta)=x_{i+1}(p_{n^{\prime}};\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>, then, by injectivity of
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m47" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> applied coordinatewise, we get:</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.5.1" class="ltx_text">Equivalently, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m48" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{i}(y_{n}-y_{n^{\prime}})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{i}(y_{n}-y_{n^{\prime}})=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m49" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{n}-y_{n^{\prime}}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{n}-y_{n^{\prime}}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, this is a
proper linear condition on the entries of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m50" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence, for fixed
previous blocks, it defines a Lebesgue-null subset of the space of
blocks <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m51" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. Taking the finite union over all pairs <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m52" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\neq n^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≠</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\neq n^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, we get
that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m53" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i+1})</annotation></semantics></math> holds for Lebesgue-a.e. block <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m54" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
It remains to pass from a fixed choice of the previous blocks to all
parameters. Write <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m55" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{k}\coloneqq d_{k+1}(d_{k}+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{k}\coloneqq d_{k+1}(d_{k}+1)</annotation></semantics></math> for the size of block
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m56" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and, for <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m57" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1\leq i\leq L-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1\leq i\leq L-2</annotation></semantics></math>, let
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m58" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{i}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q_{0}+\cdots+q_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{i}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q_{0}+\cdots+q_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the set of prefixes
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m59" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> for which <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m60" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m61" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> fails for some
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m62" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\leq i+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\leq i+1</annotation></semantics></math>; thus <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m63" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{-1}=\emptyset" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{-1}=\emptyset</annotation></semantics></math>. Each <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m64" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a
Borel set: the failure of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m65" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> is the vanishing of all
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m66" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d_{k}+1)\times(d_{k}+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d_{k}+1)\times(d_{k}+1)</annotation></semantics></math> minors of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m67" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{k}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>k</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{k}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>,
finitely many real-analytic functions of the prefix, and the failure of
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m68" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> is a finite union of equalities between real-analytic
functions. If <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m69" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i})\in\mathcal{B}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i})\in\mathcal{B}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, then either
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m70" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1})\in\mathcal{B}_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1})\in\mathcal{B}_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, or this prefix satisfies
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m71" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m72" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> belongs to the set <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m73" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1})</annotation></semantics></math> of blocks
for which <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m74" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R_{i+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R_{i+1})</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m75" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(D_{i+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(D_{i+1})</annotation></semantics></math> fails, which we have just shown to
be Lebesgue-null. Hence, by Tonelli’s theorem,</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.6.1" class="ltx_text">where the first term vanishes because <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m76" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is null by the
induction hypothesis and the second because its integrand vanishes.
Iterating this over <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m77" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=0,\ldots,L-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=0,\ldots,L-2</annotation></semantics></math>, every <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m78" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is
Lebesgue-null. Finally, since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m79" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> only involves the blocks
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m80" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{0},\ldots,B_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, the set of parameters <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m81" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}</annotation></semantics></math> for
which <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m82" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> fails for some <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m83" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{0,\cdots,L-1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{0,\cdots,L-1\}</annotation></semantics></math> is contained in
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m84" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{L-2}\times\mathbb{R}^{q_{L-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{L-2}\times\mathbb{R}^{q_{L-1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is null; its intersection
with <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m85" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the required <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p5.m86" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>. This completes
the proof.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We now prove Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem9" title="Theorem 9 (Reconstruction from hidden layer activations). ‣ When the activation is also injective and non polynomial: ‣ B.1 Identification of Analytic MLPs from Hidden Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, which is a stronger version of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 2 (Reconstruction from hidden layer activations). ‣ 3.1 Hidden probes provide useful information: ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>

non-polynomial. Consider fully connected MLPs with biases,

</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">For any real matrix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, the identity
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{\top}AA^{\top}v=\|A^{\top}v\|_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{\top}AA^{\top}v=\|A^{\top}v\|_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> shows that
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AA^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AA^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> is positive definite exactly when <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> has full
row rank. Consequently,</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text">Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma2" title="Lemma 2. ‣ When the activation is also injective and non polynomial: ‣ B.1 Identification of Analytic MLPs from Hidden Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> gives these ranks
simultaneously for Lebesgue-almost every
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}</annotation></semantics></math>. In particular, they hold at some
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, and hence <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathcal{P}}(\theta_{*})&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathcal{P}}(\theta_{*})&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> is not identically zero.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">By continuity, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> is closed and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}\leq q_{\mathbf{D}}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}\leq q_{\mathbf{D}}-1</annotation></semantics></math> since it forms the zero-set of an analytic function. Therefore <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> is Lebesgue-null. It has empty
interior, since every nonempty open subset of
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}</annotation></semantics></math> has positive Lebesgue measure. Being closed
with empty interior, it is nowhere dense.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix

By the definition of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10.2.1" class="ltx_text">If <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=\theta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=\theta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> then trivially <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">Conversely, let <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=(B_{0},\ldots,B_{L-1})\in\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=(B_{0},\ldots,B_{L-1})\in\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>. We show that <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}=B_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}=B_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> layer
by layer. Fix <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{0,\cdots,L-1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{0,\cdots,L-1\}</annotation></semantics></math>. By definition,
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})\,\text{and}\,\mathbf{X}_{i+1}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\mathbf{X}_{i+1}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐗</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\mathbf{X}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})\,\text{and}\,\mathbf{X}_{i+1}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\mathbf{X}_{i+1}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P}),</annotation></semantics></math>. The first equality gives
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta}(\mathcal{P})=\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>,
and the second equality reads
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\left(B_{i}\,\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})\right)=\sigma\left(B_{i}^{0}\,\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})\right)\,\text{entrywise.}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>entrywise.</mtext></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\left(B_{i}\,\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})\right)=\sigma\left(B_{i}^{0}\,\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})\right)\,\text{entrywise.}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is injective and applied entrywise, this implies
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})=B_{i}^{0}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})=B_{i}^{0}\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Equivalently, we have</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.3.1" class="ltx_text">is a right inverse of <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Multiplying the previous display by it on the right gives
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{i}=W_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{i}=W_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{i}=b_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{i}=b_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e. <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}=B_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}=B_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> was
arbitrary, <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta=\theta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta=\theta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})\iff\theta=\theta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⇔</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})\iff\theta=\theta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, and in
particular <math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}(\cdot,\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}(\cdot,\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> is injective on
<math id="A2.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p11.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}\setminus\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><mo>∖</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}\setminus\mathcal{M}_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
