<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Lower bounds on probe counts</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For analytic MLPs, we have established upper bounds on the number of probes required for unique function identification, using either final-layer or hidden-layer probes. We now establish nearly matching lower bounds for shallow networks. Since these lower bounds hold for one-hidden-layer networks of arbitrary width, they also provide necessary lower bounds for the general family of MLPs with analytic activations (or analytic, injective, non-polynomial activations when observing <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}</annotation></semantics></math>). The formal results are stated in Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem10" title="Theorem 10 (Tightness of probe complexities). ‣ B.2 Lower bounds on probe counts ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We now prove several lemmas needed to establish the tightness results in Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem10" title="Theorem 10 (Tightness of probe complexities). ‣ B.2 Lower bounds on probe counts ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3</span></span><span id="Thmlemma3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> be a nonzero real trigonometric polynomial
of the form <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(t)=A_{0}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(A_{k}\cos(kt)+B_{k}\sin(kt)\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(t)=A_{0}+\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(A_{k}\cos(kt)+B_{k}\sin(kt)\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, not identically <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> has at most <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2K</annotation></semantics></math> distinct zeros in <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,2\pi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,2\pi)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, suppose another nonzero sum <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> of the same form has <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2K</annotation></semantics></math> distinct zeros in <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,2\pi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,2\pi)</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes at all those points, then <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=\lambda H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=\lambda H</annotation></semantics></math> for some real number <math id="Thmlemma3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Write <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T(t)=\sum_{k=-K}^{K}c_{k}e^{ikt}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T(t)=\sum_{k=-K}^{K}c_{k}e^{ikt}</annotation></semantics></math> and define <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{T}(z)\coloneqq\sum_{k=-K}^{K}c_{k}z^{k+K}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">≔</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{T}(z)\coloneqq\sum_{k=-K}^{K}c_{k}z^{k+K}.</annotation></semantics></math>
The polynomial <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> is nonzero, has degree at most <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2K</annotation></semantics></math>, and satisfies
<math id="A2.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{T}(e^{it})=e^{iKt}T(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{T}(e^{it})=e^{iKt}T(t)</annotation></semantics></math>. Distinct zeros modulo <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> give distinct
roots of <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, proving the first assertion. For the second assertion,
<math id="A2.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{H}</annotation></semantics></math> has degree <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2K</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2K</annotation></semantics></math> distinct roots, all shared by <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{T}=\lambda P_{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>H</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{T}=\lambda P_{H}</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=\lambda H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=\lambda H</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>
real because both functions are real-valued and <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\not\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>≢</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\not\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4</span></span><span id="Thmlemma4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\{\left(S(z_{1}),\ldots,S(z_{4K})\right):S\in\mathcal{V}_{K}\right\}</annotation></semantics></math> is a <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3K</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional linear subspace of <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4K}</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover, a function <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\mathcal{V}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\mathcal{V}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies
<math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(z_{n})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(z_{n})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=1,\ldots,4K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=1,\ldots,4K</annotation></semantics></math> if and only if there exists <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(t)=\lambda H(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t)=\lambda H(t)</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="Thmlemma4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Every <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\mathcal{V}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\mathcal{V}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> can be written as
<math id="A2.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S(t)=Q(t)+tR(t),\,Q(t)=a_{0}+\sum_{k=1}^{K},\,\left(a_{k}\sin(kt)+b_{k}\cos(kt)\right),\,R(t)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}c_{k}\cos(kt)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t)=Q(t)+tR(t),\,Q(t)=a_{0}+\sum_{k=1}^{K},\,\left(a_{k}\sin(kt)+b_{k}\cos(kt)\right),\,R(t)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}c_{k}\cos(kt).</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">We first verify that these coefficients are uniquely determined
by <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>. It suffices to show that <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(t)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> forces
all coefficients to be zero. Since <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> are
<math id="A2.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>-periodic, subtracting the identity at <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> from the
identity at <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t+2\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t+2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0=S(t+2\pi)-S(t)=2\pi R(t)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0=S(t+2\pi)-S(t)=2\pi R(t).</annotation></semantics></math>
Thus <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0</annotation></semantics></math>, and then <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=0</annotation></semantics></math>. For each <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell=1,\ldots,K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell=1,\ldots,K</annotation></semantics></math>,
the elementary sine and cosine integration identities give
<math id="A2.SS2.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{0}^{2\pi}R(t)\cos(\ell t)\,dt=\pi c_{\ell},\,\int_{0}^{2\pi}Q(t)\,dt=2\pi a_{0},\,\int_{0}^{2\pi}Q(t)\sin(\ell t)\,dt=\pi stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" </div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">We next characterize the functions whose sampled values are
all zero. Suppose <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(z_{n})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(z_{n})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=1,\ldots,4K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=1,\ldots,4K</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\ldots,2K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi periodicity gives <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0=S(r_{j})=Q(r_{j})+r_{j}R(r_{j}),\,0=S(r_{j}+2\pi)=Q(r_{j})+(r_{j}+2\pi)R(r_{j})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>R</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 0</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0=S(r_{j})=Q(r_{j})+r_{j}R(r_{j}),\,0=S(r_{j}+2\pi)=Q(r_{j})+(r_{j}+2\pi)R(r_{j}).</annotation></semantics></math> Subtracting these yields <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R(r_{j})=0,\,j=1,\ldots,2K." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>K</mi><mo Since <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> is a finite cosine sum using frequencies at most
<math id="A2.SS2.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma3" title="Lemma 3. ‣ B.2 Lower bounds on probe counts ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> implies
<math id="A2.SS2.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=\mu H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=\mu H</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>; if <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0</annotation></semantics></math>, take <math id="A2.SS2.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">For every real <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, cosine symmetry and sine antisymmetry give <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(-t)=R(t),\,H(-t)=-H(t)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(-t)=R(t),\,H(-t)=-H(t).</annotation></semantics></math> Therefore we get: <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu H(t)=R(t)=R(-t)=\mu H(-t)=-\mu H(t)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu H(t)=R(t)=R(-t)=\mu H(-t)=-\mu H(t).</annotation></semantics></math>
It follows that <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\mu H(t)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\mu H(t)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. Because <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is not identically zero, <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu=0</annotation></semantics></math>, and hence <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">We now have <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=Q</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q(r_{j})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q(r_{j})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>.
A second application of Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma3" title="Lemma 3. ‣ B.2 Lower bounds on probe counts ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>
gives <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(t)=Q(t)=\lambda H(t)\,\forall\,t\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t)=Q(t)=\lambda H(t)\,\forall\,t\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, including <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=0</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Conversely, every function <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=\lambda H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=\lambda H</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes at all
<math id="A2.SS2.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{j}+2\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{j}+2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, since <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.SS2.p8.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>-periodic.
This proves the stated equivalence.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">It remains to determine the dimension of the set of sampled
vectors. For any function <math id="A2.SS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, write
<math id="A2.SS2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{\phi}\coloneqq\left(\phi(z_{1}),\ldots,\phi(z_{4K})\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{4K}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\phi}\coloneqq\left(\phi(z_{1}),\ldots,\phi(z_{4K})\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{4K}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Choose <math id="A2.SS2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{*}\in\{1,\ldots,K\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{*}\in\{1,\ldots,K\}</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="A2.SS2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{k_{*}}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub></msub><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{k_{*}}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which is possible because <math id="A2.SS2.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is not
identically zero. Consider the following collection of
<math id="A2.SS2.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3K</annotation></semantics></math> functions:</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx30" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex47.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{B}\coloneqq\{1\}\cup\{\sin(kt):1\leq k\leq K,\ k\neq k_{*}\}\cup\{\cos(kt):1\leq k\leq K\}\cup\{t\cos(kt):1\leq k\leq K\}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{B}\coloneqq\{1\}\cup\{\sin(kt):1\leq k\leq K,\ k\neq k_{*}\}\cup\{\cos(kt):1\leq k\leq K\}\cup\{t\cos(kt):1\leq k\leq K\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A2.SS2.p9.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p9.2.1" class="ltx_text">We show that their sampled vectors
<math id="A2.SS2.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{v_{\phi}:\phi\in\mathcal{B}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{v_{\phi}:\phi\in\mathcal{B}\}</annotation></semantics></math> are linearly independent
and that every sampled vector from <math id="A2.SS2.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> is a linear
combination of them.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">For independence, suppose real coefficients <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math>
satisfy <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal{B}}d_{\phi}v_{\phi}=0." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal{B}}d_{\phi}v_{\phi}=0.</annotation></semantics></math>
Define <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(t)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal{B}}d_{\phi}\phi(t)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal{B}}d_{\phi}\phi(t).</annotation></semantics></math>
Then <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\mathcal{V}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\mathcal{V}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S(z_{n})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(z_{n})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>.
The equivalence already proved implies <math id="A2.SS2.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=\lambda H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=\lambda H</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">The coefficient of <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sin(k_{*}t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(k_{*}t)</annotation></semantics></math> in the displayed expression
for <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is zero, because this function was omitted from
<math id="A2.SS2.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>. Its coefficient in <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda H</annotation></semantics></math> is
<math id="A2.SS2.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda\gamma_{k_{*}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda\gamma_{k_{*}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Uniqueness of the coefficient
representation therefore gives <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0=\lambda\gamma_{k_{*}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0=\lambda\gamma_{k_{*}}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Since <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma_{k_{*}}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub></msub><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{k_{*}}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=0</annotation></semantics></math> and hence
<math id="A2.SS2.p11.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=0</annotation></semantics></math>. The linear independence established at the beginning
of the proof now forces <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\phi}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\phi}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every
<math id="A2.SS2.p11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi\in\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi\in\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus the <math id="A2.SS2.p11.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3K</annotation></semantics></math> sampled vectors are linearly independent.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, because <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes at every point of <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒵</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="0=v_{H}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\gamma_{k}v_{\sin(k\,\cdot)}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>H</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>K</mi></msup><mi>γ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.392em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0=v_{H}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\gamma_{k}v_{\sin(k\,\cdot)}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Solving for the sampled vector of the omitted sine function
gives <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="v_{\sin(k_{*}\,\cdot)}=-\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}k=1\\
k\neq k_{*}\end{subarray}}^{K}\frac{\gamma_{k}}{\gamma_{k_{*}}}v_{\sin(k\,\cdot)}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mo>∑</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>K</mi></msup><mfrac><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>γ</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub></msub></mfrac><mi>v</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.392em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{\sin(k_{*}\,\cdot)}=-\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}k=1\\
k\neq k_{*}\end{subarray}}^{K}\frac{\gamma_{k}}{\gamma_{k_{*}}}v_{\sin(k\,\cdot)}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Every function in <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> is a linear combination of
the functions in <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> and this one omitted sine
function. The last identity therefore shows that every
sampled vector from <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math> is a linear combination
of <math id="A2.SS2.p12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{v_{\phi}:\phi\in\mathcal{B}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{v_{\phi}:\phi\in\mathcal{B}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text">Conversely, every linear combination of these sampled vectors
is obtained by sampling the corresponding linear combination
of functions in <math id="A2.SS2.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>, which belongs to <math id="A2.SS2.p13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence the set of sampled vectors is exactly the linear
subspace generated by these <math id="A2.SS2.p13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3K</annotation></semantics></math> linearly independent vectors.
Its dimension is therefore <math id="A2.SS2.p13.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3K</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 5</span></span><span id="Thmlemma5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> be a nonempty open interval. If <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{j}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{j}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math> for
all <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in[m]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in[m]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{j}/w_{j}\neq b_{k}/w_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{j}/w_{j}\neq b_{k}/w_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> whenever <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\neq k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\neq k</annotation></semantics></math>, then
<math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,\tanh(w_{1}x+b_{1}),\ldots,\tanh(w_{m}x+b_{m})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>tanh</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>tanh</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,\tanh(w_{1}x+b_{1}),\ldots,\tanh(w_{m}x+b_{m})</annotation></semantics></math> are linearly independent
on <math id="Thmlemma5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p14" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p14.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p14.1.1" class="ltx_text">Suppose <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C+\sum_{j=1}^{m}A_{j}\tanh(w_{j}x+b_{j})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>tanh</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C+\sum_{j=1}^{m}A_{j}\tanh(w_{j}x+b_{j})=0</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Extend the left-hand side to the meromorphic function</span></p>

Their real part is <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="-b_{j}/w_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-b_{j}/w_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, so no
pole is shared by two distinct summands. The union of the pole sets
is closed and discrete, and its complement in <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℂ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}</annotation></semantics></math> is connected:
a segment between any two points can be detoured around the finitely
many poles it meets. By the Identity Theorem of complex analysis, <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi</annotation></semantics></math> is zero on this
complement because it vanishes on <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>. Its residue at every pole
therefore vanishes. Thus <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{j}/w_{j}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{j}/w_{j}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{j}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{j}=0</annotation></semantics></math>
and then <math id="A2.SS2.p14.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 10</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Tightness of probe complexities)<span id="Thmtheorem10.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Thmtheorem10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(u,\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(u,\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> denote a shallow universal MLP, with analytic activation <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, and layers of dimension <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}=(1,m,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}=(1,m,1)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, the total number of parameters is <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q=3m+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q=3m+1</annotation></semantics></math> and the maximal dimension of any layer is <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\max}=m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\max}=m</annotation></semantics></math>. In each of the following cases, there exists
a compact parameter space <math id="Thmtheorem10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q}</annotation></semantics></math>
with nonempty interior for which the stated conclusion holds. We have the following:</span></p>
<ol id="A2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There exists a real-analytic activation </span><math id="A2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=\sin</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text <div id="A2.SS2.5" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p15.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p15.1.1" class="ltx_text">We start with two observations:</span></p>
<ul id="A2.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To show that the lower bound of <math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q-1</annotation></semantics></math> is necessary for the family of all MLPs with analytic activations, it is sufficient to come up with one analytic activation for which the <math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q-2</annotation></semantics></math> probes don’t suffice. We use <math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=\sin" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=\sin</annotation></semantics></math> in part 1 and <math id="A2.I2.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>tanh</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=\tanh</annotation></semantics></math> in part 2.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We show the necessary lower bounds <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q-1</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\max}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\max}+1</annotation></semantics></math> using the layer widths <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}=(1,m,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}=(1,m,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, but we show the tightness for any <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\in\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\in\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math>. Now by taking <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> we can conclude the general lower bound of <math id="A2.I2.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q-1</annotation></semantics></math> is tight.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A2.SS2.p15.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p15.2.1" class="ltx_text">With these arguments, we now prove the two constructive counter examples that establish the lower bounds.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p16" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p16.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p16.1.1" class="ltx_text">We start with proving the first part. First we consider an interval containing <math id="A2.SS2.p16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,4\pi]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,4\pi]</annotation></semantics></math>.
We set <math id="A2.SS2.p16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\coloneqq 2m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\coloneqq 2m</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS2.p16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\coloneqq 1/(100m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\coloneqq 1/(100m)</annotation></semantics></math>, and choose base
parameters <math id="A2.SS2.p16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{1}^{0},\theta_{2}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{1}^{0},\theta_{2}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> whose affine pre-activations are</span></p>
