the remaining <math id="A2.SS2.p19.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q-N_{0}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q-N_{0}=2</annotation></semantics></math> parameter coordinates at their base values.
The implicit function theorem gives parameter pairs
<math id="A2.SS2.p19.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{1}(\mathcal{P}),\theta_{2}(\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{1}(\mathcal{P}),\theta_{2}(\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>, continuous on a nonempty open
neighborhood <math id="A2.SS2.p19.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A2.SS2.p19.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, such that <math id="A2.SS2.p19.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}(\theta_{1}(\mathcal{P}),\theta_{2}(\mathcal{P}),\mathcal{P})=0\,\forall\,\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">∀</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}(\theta_{1}(\mathcal{P}),\theta_{2}(\mathcal{P}),\mathcal{P})=0\,\forall\,\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Consequently their final sine outputs agree at every probe.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p20" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p20.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p20.1.1" class="ltx_text">Choose <math id="A2.SS2.p20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{*}\in(0,4\pi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{*}\in(0,4\pi)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS2.p20.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(t_{*})\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(t_{*})\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math>. At the base pair, we have <math id="A2.SS2.p20.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|g_{1}(t)|\leq m\epsilon&lt;\pi/2,\,|g_{2}(t)|\leq 1+(m-1)\epsilon&lt;\pi/2." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|g_{1}(t)|\leq m\epsilon&lt;\pi/2,\,|g_{2}(t)|\leq 1+(m-1)\epsilon&lt;\pi/2.</annotation></semantics></math>
The sine function is injective on <math id="A2.SS2.p20.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(-\pi/2,\pi/2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-\pi/2,\pi/2)</annotation></semantics></math>, so
<math id="A2.SS2.p20.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(t_{*};\theta_{1}^{0})\neq f(t_{*};\theta_{2}^{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(t_{*};\theta_{1}^{0})\neq f(t_{*};\theta_{2}^{0})</annotation></semantics></math>. We shrink the neighbourhood
<math id="A2.SS2.p20.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> so that this inequality persists, the probe
entries remain distinct, and both parameter vectors lie in compact
boxes around their base values with positive distinct slopes and
nonzero readout coefficients. Their union is a compact set
<math id="A2.SS2.p20.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{K}</annotation></semantics></math> with nonempty interior containing every constructed pair.
Thus the final functions are different for every tuple in this open set.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p21" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p21.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p21.1.1" class="ltx_text">For a general interval <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, choose <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[a,b]\subset\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[a,b]\subset\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&lt;b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&lt;b</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="A2.SS2.p21.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=\alpha x+\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=\alpha x+\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, mapping <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[a,b]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[a,b]</annotation></semantics></math> onto <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,4\pi]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,4\pi]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Replacing each hidden row <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(w_{j},b_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(w_{j},b_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> by
<math id="A2.SS2.p21.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha w_{j},\beta w_{j}+b_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha w_{j},\beta w_{j}+b_{j})</annotation></semantics></math> is an invertible linear change of its
parameters. It transports the construction, its open probe set, and
the compact parameter set into <math id="A2.SS2.p21.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p22" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p22.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p22.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="A2.SS2.p22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N&lt;N_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N&lt;N_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A2.SS2.p22.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> be the projection of
<math id="A2.SS2.p22.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> onto the first <math id="A2.SS2.p22.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> probe coordinates. This set
is nonempty and open. Every tuple in <math id="A2.SS2.p22.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> extends to a
tuple in <math id="A2.SS2.p22.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{N_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math>, whose colliding pair also agrees on
the shorter tuple and belongs to the same <math id="A2.SS2.p22.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{K}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since a
nonempty open set has positive Lebesgue measure, generic shared
separation is impossible for <math id="A2.SS2.p22.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\leq 2q-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\leq 2q-2</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p23" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p23.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p23.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now we prove the second part. Fix any
<math id="A2.SS2.p23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{0}=(w,b,a,c)\in\operatorname{int}(\Theta_{\mathbf{D}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>int</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{0}=(w,b,a,c)\in\operatorname{int}(\Theta_{\mathbf{D}})</annotation></semantics></math>
such that <math id="A2.SS2.p23.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{j}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{j}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS2.p23.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS2.p23.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{j}w_{k}-b_{k}w_{j}\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{j}w_{k}-b_{k}w_{j}\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math> whenever <math id="A2.SS2.p23.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j&lt;k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j&lt;k</annotation></semantics></math>.
These conditions hold for Lebesgue-almost every interior
parameter, because their failure is a finite union of zero sets
of nonzero polynomials.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p24" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p24.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p24.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A2.SS2.p24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq N\leq m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq N\leq m</annotation></semantics></math> and an arbitrary probe tuple <math id="A2.SS2.p24.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{X}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{X}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The matrix</span></p>

and <math id="A2.SS2.p26.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta(t)\to\theta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta(t)\to\theta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus all sufficiently small
nonzero <math id="A2.SS2.p26.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> give parameters in <math id="A2.SS2.p26.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}</annotation></semantics></math> and in
any prescribed neighborhood of <math id="A2.SS2.p26.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This proves that, for every probe tuple with <math id="A2.SS2.p26.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\leq m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\leq m</annotation></semantics></math>,
almost every interior target admits arbitrarily close,
functionally distinct competitors with identical complete
probe observations.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS2.p27" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p27.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p27.1.1" class="ltx_text">For this shallow <math id="A2.SS2.p27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>tanh</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh</annotation></semantics></math> family, <math id="A2.SS2.p27.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\max}=m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\max}=m</annotation></semantics></math> hidden probes
fail to identify almost every interior target, whereas the
upper bound guarantees identification of almost every target
from almost every tuple of <math id="A2.SS2.p27.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{\max}+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{\max}+1</annotation></semantics></math> probes.
Thus the hidden-probe threshold is sharp in the worst case
over the class of analytic, injective, non-polynomial activations.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p28" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p28.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p28.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the <math id="A2.SS2.p28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sin" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>sin</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin</annotation></semantics></math> family, the nonempty open set of failing
probe tuples at <math id="A2.SS2.p28.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\leq 2q-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\leq 2q-2</annotation></semantics></math> rules out a general
almost-everywhere-in-probes identification guarantee at
those cardinalities. Hence the sufficient bound <math id="A2.SS2.p28.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q+1</annotation></semantics></math>
is within two probes of the lower bound <math id="A2.SS2.p28.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2q-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2q-1</annotation></semantics></math> for such
a guarantee. We do not claim that these bounds are tight
for every individual activation.
∎</span></p>

<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>ReLU Network Identification from probes</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We begin with a counterexample showing that ReLU networks cannot be exactly reconstructed from finitely many probes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">See <a href="#Thmtheorem3" title="Proposition 3 (Finite probes do not identify ReLU networks). ‣ 3.2 Identifying ReLU Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Consider hat functions of the form</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex64" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="A2.SS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">For any <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c,\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c,\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, such a function is a <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ReLU}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ReLU</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ReLU}</annotation></semantics></math> network with three hidden neurons, and it is supported in <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[c-\epsilon,c+\epsilon]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[c-\epsilon,c+\epsilon]</annotation></semantics></math>. Given any probes
<math id="A2.SS3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},\cdots,p_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},\cdots,p_{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, choose <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> off the probes and
<math id="A2.SS3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\epsilon_{1}&lt;\epsilon_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\epsilon_{1}&lt;\epsilon_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> below the distance from <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> to the probes and to
the boundary; then <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\epsilon_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\epsilon_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\epsilon_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\epsilon_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> vanish at every
probe and differ at <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus no finite set of probes, however chosen, can completely identify <math id="A2.SS3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ReLU}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ReLU</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ReLU}</annotation></semantics></math> networks.
∎</span></p>
</div>

<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The probabilistic setting of identification:</h5>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Here we describe the probabilistic setting of function identification in ReLU Nets. Let <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> be a Borel
probability measure on <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>. The probes are drawn
from <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu,\,\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\cdots,p_{N})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu,\,\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\cdots,p_{N})</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},\cdots,p_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},\cdots,p_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> i.i.d. <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math>. We also consider the same measure to quantify agreement between functions. For two parameters <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{0},\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{0},\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}</annotation></semantics></math> we define the disagreement sets:</p>

<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">as the measure of the inputs at which the two networks compute different
outputs. For uniform <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> these are
fractions of the volume of <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>. Given thresholds <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon,\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon,\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we consider guarantees of the form: for every target <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, with probability at least <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math> over the probes, every network <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(\cdot,\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\cdot,\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> agreeing on those probes also agrees with <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(\cdot,\theta_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\cdot,\theta_{0})</annotation></semantics></math> outside a set of measure at most <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>. If we moreover assume that <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sup_{\theta\in\Theta,x\in\mathcal{X}}\|f(x;\theta)\|\leq B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>sup</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sup_{\theta\in\Theta,x\in\mathcal{X}}\|f(x;\theta)\|\leq B</annotation></semantics></math> for some constant <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, then we would like to show that one can reconstruct <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> up to any <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{s}(\mu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>s</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{s}(\mu)</annotation></semantics></math> norm. Note that such boundedness assumption is automatic for the hypothesis class of ReLU networks if we assume the input space <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and the parameter space <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta</annotation></semantics></math> to be compact.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4 (semi-formal-PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ 3.2 Identifying ReLU Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> presents a semi-formal version of our results for ReLU networks, while Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem11" title="Theorem 11 (PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ Proof of the formal version of Theorem : ‣ B.3 ReLU Network Identification from probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> provides the formal statement. Intuitively, this theorem says the following. Since we cannot identify the function <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly everywhere from the probes, we want to identify <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> at a large region of the input space <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, namely at a set of measure at least <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> (where <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(\mathcal{X})=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(\mathcal{X})=1</annotation></semantics></math>) by using <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> many probes. Also assuming that the probes are sampled independently at random under the same probability measure <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math>, we want the above property to hold with high probability (at least <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>). Thus, we want the target function <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> and the reconstructed function <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\hat{\theta}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\hat{\theta}}</annotation></semantics></math> to be approximately equal with high probability. This is similar in spirit (but unrelated) to the PAC learning framework used in classical learning theory. Now, we prove Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem11" title="Theorem 11 (PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ Proof of the formal version of Theorem : ‣ B.3 ReLU Network Identification from probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> on <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ReLU}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ReLU</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ReLU}</annotation></semantics></math> networks, which is a formal version of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4 (semi-formal-PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ 3.2 Identifying ReLU Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. For that we first define some notations and prove a couple of helper lemmas.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Proof of the formal version of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4 (semi-formal-PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ 3.2 Identifying ReLU Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>:</h5>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first state and prove some bounds on counting polynomials and the
random-sampling bound used in the proof. The zero-pattern estimate below is a specialization of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rónyai et al. (2001, Theorem 1.1)</a></cite>.
We still prove it for completeness.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 6</span></span><span id="Thmlemma6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Counting polynomial tests)<span id="Thmlemma6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{1},\cdots,g_{J}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>J</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{1},\cdots,g_{J}</annotation></semantics></math> be real polynomials of degree at most <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>
in <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> variables, where <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P,r,J\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P,r,J\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and we define
<math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\coloneqq\binom{P+r}{r}-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\coloneqq\binom{P+r}{r}-1</annotation></semantics></math>.
The numbers of distinct vectors
<math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\left(\mathbf{1}[g_{j}(v)&gt;0]\right)_{j=1}^{J},\,\left(\mathbf{1}[g_{j}(v)\neq 0]\right)_{j=1}^{J},\,v\in\mathbb{R}^{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>J</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>J</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>P</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\mathbf{1}[g_{j}(v)&gt;0]\right)_{j=1}^{J},\,\left(\mathbf{1}[g_{j}(v)\neq 0]\right)_{j=1}^{J},\,v\in\mathbb{R}^{P}</annotation></semantics></math>,
are at most <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em">(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>J</mi><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\binom{P+rJ}{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>P</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\binom{P+rJ}{P}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively.
If <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J\geq D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J\geq D</annotation></semantics></math>, the first bound is at most <math id="Thmlemma6.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(eJ/D)^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>D</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(eJ/D)^{D}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We first bound the number of positive vectors. For this, we choose one parameter for each realized vector. Subtract from every <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> a positive number smaller
than all its positive values at the chosen parameters.
If none of these values is positive, any positive number works.
This preserves every chosen binary vector and makes all
tested values nonzero.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">List the <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> nonconstant monomials of degree at most <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>.
Each shifted polynomial is an affine function of this list.
It remains to count strict sign vectors of <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> affine
functions on <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math>. A nonempty set with fixed strict
signs is an intersection of open halfspaces and is convex.
Adding one zero hyperplane splits such a set only when
the hyperplane meets it. The intersections of the split
sets with this hyperplane have distinct strict sign
vectors for the preceding functions restricted to
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{D-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{D-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. A repeated hyperplane causes no split,
and constant functions add no choices.
Thus the maximum count <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(J,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>J</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(J,D)</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx39" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex65"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex65.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle a(J,D)\leq a(J-1,D)+a(J-1,D-1)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>J</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle a(J,D)\leq a(J-1,D)+a(J-1,D-1).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Starting from <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(0,D)=a(J,0)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>J</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(0,D)=a(J,0)=1</annotation></semantics></math>, induction gives
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(J,D)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>J</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">≤</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>J</mi><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(J,D)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J\geq D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J\geq D</annotation></semantics></math>, we set <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=D/J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=D/J</annotation></semantics></math> and we conclude by the following bounding:</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx40" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex66"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex66.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle t^{D}\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}\leq\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}t^{k}\leq(1+t)^{J}\leq e^{D}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>D</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>J</mi><mi>k</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>D</mi></munderover></mstyle><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mi>J</mi><mi>k</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>J</mi></msup><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle t^{D}\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}\leq\sum_{k=0}^{D}\binom{J}{k}t^{k}\leq(1+t)^{J}\leq e^{D}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now we bound the number of non-zero vectors. Let <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> contain the realized
sets <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{j:g_{j}(v)\neq 0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{j:g_{j}(v)\neq 0\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We choose a realizing parameter <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> for each
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, and define <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{S}\coloneqq\prod_{j\in S}g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">≔</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{S}\coloneqq\prod_{j\in S}g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>,
with empty product <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{S}(v_{T})\neq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{S}(v_{T})\neq 0</annotation></semantics></math> exactly when <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\subseteq T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\subseteq T</annotation></semantics></math>.
Ordering the sets by nondecreasing cardinality makes the matrix
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(G_{S}(v_{T}))_{S,T\in\mathcal{S}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(G_{S}(v_{T}))_{S,T\in\mathcal{S}}</annotation></semantics></math> upper triangular
with nonzero diagonal. The polynomials <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{S}</annotation></semantics></math> are therefore
linearly independent. Each has degree at most <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="rJ" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">rJ</annotation></semantics></math>,
and the space of such polynomials has
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\binom{P+rJ}{P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>P</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\binom{P+rJ}{P}</annotation></semantics></math> monomials as a basis.
This proves the second bound.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For a class <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> of subsets of <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, write
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(M)</annotation></semantics></math> for the largest number of distinct
vectors <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(\mathbf{1}[p_{a}\in C])_{a=1}^{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>M</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{1}[p_{a}\in C])_{a=1}^{M}</annotation></semantics></math>, as <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\in\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\in\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math>
varies, on any <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> fixed inputs. This is the growth function of <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> from VC theory. Moreover, the following lemma is inspired from the classical
double-sampling argument for random <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>-nets from
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Haussler and Welzl, 1987</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Blumer et al., 1989</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We also use the following consequence of the polynomial
sign bound of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bartlett et al. (2019, Lemma 17)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 7</span></span><span id="Thmlemma7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Counting polynomial inequalities)<span id="Thmlemma7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{1},\cdots,g_{J}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>J</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{1},\cdots,g_{J}</annotation></semantics></math> be real polynomials of degree at most

Then</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">Choose one parameter for each realized binary vector.
For each <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, choose <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{j}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{j}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> smaller than every
positive value of <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> at these finitely many parameters;
if there is no positive value, choose any <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{j}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{j}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Replacing <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}-\eta_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}-\eta_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> preserves the chosen
binary vectors and makes every tested value nonzero.
The polynomial sign bound therefore gives at most</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text">such vectors.
∎</span></p>

<div id="Thmlemma8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 8</span></span><span id="Thmlemma8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Random samples detect large disagreement sets)<span id="Thmlemma8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K,\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K,\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> be compact metric spaces, let <math id="Thmlemma8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> be a Borel

has <math id="Thmlemma8.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(C)\leq\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(C)\leq\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> be the event that the sample misses some <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>
with <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(C)&gt;\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(C)&gt;\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>. Draw an independent second
sample of size <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>E</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> be the event that some
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\in\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\in\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> contains no first-sample point and at
least <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\epsilon/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\epsilon/2</annotation></semantics></math> second-sample points.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">These events are measurable. To see this, we observe that the map
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\mapsto\mu(C_{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\mapsto\mu(C_{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math> is lower semicontinuous by
Fatou’s lemma. In <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\times\mathcal{X}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\times\mathcal{X}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\times\mathcal{X}^{2N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\times\mathcal{X}^{2N}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the no-hit conditions are closed, whereas the conditions
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(C_{\theta})&gt;\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(C_{\theta})&gt;\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> and the required number of
second-sample hits are open. The defining sets are
therefore intersections of a closed set with an open
set in a compact metric space. Such sets are countable
unions of compact sets, as are their coordinate
projections onto the samples. Thus <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E,E^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>E</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E,E^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> are Borel.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">Suppose the first sample belongs to <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math>, and choose
a witnessing set of measure <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q&gt;\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q&gt;\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.
Its second-sample hit count <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> has mean <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Nq" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Nq</annotation></semantics></math> and
variance <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Nq(1-q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Nq(1-q)</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\epsilon\geq 8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\epsilon\geq 8</annotation></semantics></math>, by Chebyshev’s
inequality we get</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx45" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex71"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex71.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\{Z&lt;N\epsilon/2\}\leq\frac{4(1-q)}{Nq}&lt;\frac{1}{2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>N</mi><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>&lt;</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{P}\{Z&lt;N\epsilon/2\}\leq\frac{4(1-q)}{Nq}&lt;\frac{1}{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.2.1" class="ltx_text">Consequently we have <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}(E)\leq 2\mathbb{P}(E^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>E</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}(E)\leq 2\mathbb{P}(E^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now we pair the two samples and independently swap the members
of each pair with probability <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/2</annotation></semantics></math>. Their joint distribution
is unchanged. On the fixed <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2N</annotation></semantics></math> points there are at
most <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(2N)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(2N)</annotation></semantics></math> membership vectors.
For a fixed vector to witness <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>E</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, all its marked
points must be assigned to the second sample.
If a pair has two marked points this is impossible;
otherwise, with <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> marked points, its probability is
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{-k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{-k}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\geq N\epsilon/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\geq N\epsilon/2</annotation></semantics></math>, a union bound gives
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p11.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{P}(E)\leq 2\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(2N)2^{-N\epsilon/2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>N</mi><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}(E)\leq 2\Pi_{\mathcal{C}}(2N)2^{-N\epsilon/2}.</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text">It remains to check the stated threshold.
Put <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A=D\log(12eQ/\epsilon)+\log(2/\delta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Q</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A=D\log(12eQ/\epsilon)+\log(2/\delta)</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{0}=6A/\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{0}=6A/\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{0}&gt;D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{0}&gt;D</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{0}\epsilon&gt;8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{0}\epsilon&gt;8</annotation></semantics></math>, and</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.2.1" class="ltx_text">The function

Hence, for every such <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
