<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.3.1" class="ltx_text">Applying the growth bound at <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=2N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=2N</annotation></semantics></math> and using
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p12.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3\log 2/2&gt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\log 2/2&gt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, we conclude that</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx48" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p13.1" class="ltx_p">We shall now state and prove Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem11" title="Theorem 11 (PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ Proof of the formal version of Theorem : ‣ B.3 ReLU Network Identification from probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>, which is the formal version of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4 (semi-formal-PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ 3.2 Identifying ReLU Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. Throughout this section, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> is compact, <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=\mathrm{ReLU}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>ReLU</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=\mathrm{ReLU}</annotation></semantics></math> in layers <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p13.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1,\cdots,L-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,\cdots,L-1</annotation></semantics></math> and the output layer is
linear. We use the following notations for ReLU nets, similar to what we used for analytic nets:</p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 11</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(PAC identification of <math id="Thmtheorem11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ReLU}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ReLU</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ReLU}</annotation></semantics></math> networks)<span id="Thmtheorem11.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem11.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Thmtheorem11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> be compact and <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>μ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu</annotation></semantics></math> be a Borel probability measure on <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>. Consider the family of <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ReLU}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ReLU</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ReLU}</annotation></semantics></math> MLPs <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> neurons with widths <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{D}\coloneqq(d,d_{1},\cdots,d_{L-1},m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{D}\coloneqq(d,d_{1},\cdots,d_{L-1},m)</annotation></semantics></math> with compact parameter space <math id="Thmtheorem11.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q_{\mathbf{D}}}</annotation></semantics></math>. in <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Each equality <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=0</annotation></semantics></math> is determined by the

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p17" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p17.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p17.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now consider final-output observations. We count the
hidden activation patterns successively over the layers,
as in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bartlett et al. (2019, Section 4)</a></cite>.

For <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p17.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=0,\cdots,L-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=0,\cdots,L-1</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p17.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> be the partition
of <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p17.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>𝐃</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{\mathbf{D}}</annotation></semantics></math> obtained by grouping parameters
according to the bits</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in[L-1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in[L-1]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\mathcal{S}_{i-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\mathcal{S}_{i-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
On <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>, every preceding ReLU equals multiplication by
its fixed activation bit at each sampled input.
Consequently, each <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i,j}(p_{a};\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i,j}(p_{a};\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> agrees on <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>
with a polynomial of degree at most <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> in the first
<math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p18.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> parameters. Indeed, first-layer preactivations
are affine, and each subsequent affine layer increases
the degree by at most one.</span></p>

probability at least <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p24.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, every

<math id="alg2.l9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i,j\in[d]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i,j\in[d]</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg2.l10" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">10:</span>
              
              
            <span id="alg2.l10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg2.l10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathbf{M},\mathbf{W})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐌</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐖</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathbf{M},\mathbf{W})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the architecture, parameter spaces, and probe maps
defined in equations <a href="#S4.E2" title="In 4 Identifying Multi-Head Attention from Probes ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>–(<a href="#S4.E3" title="In 4 Identifying Multi-Head Attention from Probes ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).
In particular, <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta</annotation></semantics></math> is the raw parameter space and
<math id="A2.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=\dim\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=\dim\Theta</annotation></semantics></math>.
The <em id="A2.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">canonical representation</em> of a layer is obtained
by merging heads with identical score matrices <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{M}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{M}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>,
summing their value matrices <math id="A2.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>, and removing groups
whose summed value matrix is zero.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We start the section with a brief discussion on related works and then prove our results.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relation to query-based attention recovery.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Query based recovery of attention blocks has been studied recently and we acknowledge the progress of those works and discuss what we contribute. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bhattamishra et al. (2026)</a></cite> study recovery of single-head
attention from scalar-output queries, while
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim and Kim (2026)</a></cite> recover canonical multi-head representations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our three-token separation argument is a matrix-output
adaptation of the canonical-identifiability result
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim and Kim, 2026</a>, Proposition 3.1)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">However, our main focus is generic identification of multilayer MHA stacks
from a shared, nonadaptive probe probes with hidden access.
We also consider different observation models: our queries return complete
tokenwise layer outputs for <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas their attention oracles
return a scalar at the final token only.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Softmax attention setup:</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Now we setup some detailed notation, some of which overlap with the same from main text, but in more details.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We begin with some definitions. We consider <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> dimensional inputs and <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> attention heads, with <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\mid d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\mid d</annotation></semantics></math>. Set <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=d/h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=d/h</annotation></semantics></math>, the value
dimension of each head, and let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> be the query/key
dimension with <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq d</annotation></semantics></math> . A bias-free, unmasked MHA layer
has parameters <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\coloneqq\{(\mathbf{Q}_{a},\mathbf{K}_{a},\mathbf{V}_{a},\mathbf{O}_{a})\}_{a=1}^{h},\,\mathbf{Q}_{a},\mathbf{K}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times k},\,\mathbf{V}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},\,\mathbf{O}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>≔</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐐</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐊</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐕</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐎</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>𝐐</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐊</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐕</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐎</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\coloneqq\{(\mathbf{Q}_{a},\mathbf{K}_{a},\mathbf{V}_{a},\mathbf{O}_{a})\}_{a=1}^{h},\,\mathbf{Q}_{a},\mathbf{K}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times k},\,\mathbf{V}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},\,\mathbf{O}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}.</annotation></semantics></math>
For an input probe <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> whose rows are the
token vectors <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}^{\top},\ldots,p_{n}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}^{\top},\ldots,p_{n}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, the layer computes</p>
<table id="A2.Ex92" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex92.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{n}(P;\theta)=\sum_{a=1}^{h}\operatorname{softmax}(P\mathbf{M}_{a}P^{\top})\,P\mathbf{W}_{a},\,\mathbf{M}_{a}\coloneqq\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{a}\mathbf{K}_{a}^{\top}}{\sqrt{k}},\,\mathbf{W}_{a}\coloneqq\mathbf{V}_{a}\mathbf{O}_{a}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>h</mi></munderover><mrow><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>𝐐</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐊</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><msqrt><mi>k</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐕</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐎</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{n}(P;\theta)=\sum_{a=1}^{h}\operatorname{softmax}(P\mathbf{M}_{a}P^{\top})\,P\mathbf{W}_{a},\,\mathbf{M}_{a}\coloneqq\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{a}\mathbf{K}_{a}^{\top}}{\sqrt{k}},\,\mathbf{W}_{a}\coloneqq\mathbf{V}_{a}\mathbf{O}_{a}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The softmax acts rowwise:<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left[\operatorname{softmax}(P\mathbf{M}_{a}P^{\top})\right]_{ij}=\frac{\exp(p_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{M}_{a}p_{j})}{\sum_{s=1}^{n}\exp(p_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{M}_{a}p_{s})}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>P</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msubsup><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[\operatorname{softmax}(P\mathbf{M}_{a}P^{\top})\right]_{ij}=\frac{\exp(p_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{M}_{a}p_{j})}{\sum_{s=1}^{n}\exp(p_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{M}_{a}p_{s})}.</annotation></semantics></math>
The matrices <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{M}_{a},\mathbf{W}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{M}_{a},\mathbf{W}_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> thus have ranks at most <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>,
respectively. A probe specifies <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> and returns the complete matrix
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{n}(P;\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{n}(P;\theta)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}</annotation></semantics></math>. An <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>-layer MHA stack has parameters
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\theta}=(\theta_{1},\ldots,\theta_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\theta}=(\theta_{1},\ldots,\theta_{L})</annotation></semantics></math> and we consider the case where the token dimension <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is preserved across layers. Layer <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> has <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> heads, query/key dimension <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>, and value dimension
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\ell}=d/h_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\ell}=d/h_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. Our proofs only need manifold doms of parameters.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta=\prod_{\ell=1}^{L}\Theta_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta=\prod_{\ell=1}^{L}\Theta_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the parameter space of the <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>-layer MHA architecture, with <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> being the parameter space of the <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>-th layer. Let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\ell}\coloneqq h_{\ell}\left(k_{\ell}(2d-k_{\ell})+r_{\ell}(2d-r_{\ell})\right),\,q\coloneqq\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}q_{\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">≔</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\ell}\coloneqq h_{\ell}\left(k_{\ell}(2d-k_{\ell})+r_{\ell}(2d-r_{\ell})\right),\,q\coloneqq\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}q_{\ell}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\ell}=\dim(\Theta_{\ell})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">dim</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\ell}=\dim(\Theta_{\ell})</annotation></semantics></math> since the set of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\times d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\times d</annotation></semantics></math> matrices of rank at most <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is an irreducible algebraic variety of dimension <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k(2d-k)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k(2d-k)</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim(\Theta_{\ell})=q_{\ell},\,\dim(\Theta)=q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">dim</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.059em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">dim</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim(\Theta_{\ell})=q_{\ell},\,\dim(\Theta)=q</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Proof of Stronger version of Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 5 (Structured probing for softmax attention). ‣ 4 Identifying Multi-Head Attention from Probes ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a></h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use two elementary facts: a discrete subset of a Euclidean
space is countable, and a nonzero analytic function on a connected
open subset of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{m}</annotation></semantics></math> has a zero set of Hausdorff dimension at
most <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m-1</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 9</span></span><span id="Thmlemma9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Three-token separation)<span id="Thmlemma9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Two MHA layers agree on every three-token input if and only if they agree
at every sequence length.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}:\rho(t)=e^{t}/(2+e^{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>ℝ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}:\rho(t)=e^{t}/(2+e^{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. It is not hard to see that the functions <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(gt)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(gt)</annotation></semantics></math> for distinct “rates” <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> are linearly independent.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now, suppose the three-token maps agree. Equal-token inputs give
equal value sums. List their distinct score matrices as <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>,
and let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> be the difference between the associated
value sums. The repeated-token row of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q+tv,q,q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q+tv,q,q)</annotation></semantics></math> then gives
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{j}\rho(tq^{\top}B_{j}v)\,v^{\top}\Delta_{j}=0." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{j}\rho(tq^{\top}B_{j}v)\,v^{\top}\Delta_{j}=0.</annotation></semantics></math>
For generic <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q,v)</annotation></semantics></math> the rates are distinct, since
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\top}(B_{j}-B_{j^{\prime}})v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\top}(B_{j}-B_{j^{\prime}})v</annotation></semantics></math> is a nonzero polynomial for <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\neq j^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≠</mo><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\neq j^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Linear independence gives <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{\top}\Delta_{j}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{\top}\Delta_{j}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, hence <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{j}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{j}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
The converse, at every length, follows by merging the summands.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We make a note that the above is the matrix-output counterpart of
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim and Kim (2026, Proposition 3.1)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 10</span></span><span id="Thmlemma10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Countably many candidates from a fixed probe batch)<span id="Thmlemma10.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Thmlemma10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\mid d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\mid d</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=d/H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=d/H</annotation></semantics></math>. Consider probe tuples
containing <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(2H+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d(2H+1)</annotation></semantics></math> probes: <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> singletons,
<math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(H+1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d(H+1)</annotation></semantics></math> triples, and <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d(H-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d(H-1)</annotation></semantics></math> sequences of length <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s+1</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="Thmlemma10.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> be the set of all such probes.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma10.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Thmlemma10.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma10.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix an MHA layer with <math id="Thmlemma10.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\leq H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\leq H</annotation></semantics></math> heads, <math id="Thmlemma10.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\mid d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\mid d</annotation></semantics></math>,
query/key dimension <math id="Thmlemma10.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq k\leq d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq k\leq d</annotation></semantics></math>, and value dimension <math id="Thmlemma10.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=d/h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=d/h</annotation></semantics></math>.
Its effective parameter space is</span></p>

<p id="Thmlemma10.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma10.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">with</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex94" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="Thmlemma10.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma10.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma10.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then, for almost all tuples <math id="Thmlemma10.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathcal{P},\theta)\in\mathbf{P}_{0}\times\Theta_{\mathrm{eff}}\setminus\mathcal{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∖</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathcal{P},\theta)\in\mathbf{P}_{0}\times\Theta_{\mathrm{eff}}\setminus\mathcal{N}</annotation></semantics></math> (with <math id="Thmlemma10.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{N}\leq\dim\mathbf{P}_{0}+q-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{N}\leq\dim\mathbf{P}_{0}+q-1</annotation></semantics></math>) and almost all <math id="Thmlemma10.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta\in\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta\in\theta_{\mathrm{eff}}</annotation></semantics></math> the set
<math id="Thmlemma10.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\{\theta^{\prime}\in\Theta_{\mathrm{eff}}:\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta^{\prime},\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})\right\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>eff</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">final</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">final</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\{\theta^{\prime}\in\Theta_{\mathrm{eff}}:\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta^{\prime},\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})\right\}</annotation></semantics></math>
is at most countable.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">We first choose parameters and probes for which no nonzero
first-order change in the parameters leaves all outputs unchanged.
We then show that this property holds almost everywhere and
implies the claimed countability.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{ij}=\alpha_{i}^{j-1},\,0&lt;\alpha_{1}&lt;\cdots&lt;\alpha_{d}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">&lt;</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">&lt;</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{ij}=\alpha_{i}^{j-1},\,0&lt;\alpha_{1}&lt;\cdots&lt;\alpha_{d},</annotation></semantics></math>
and let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> keep the <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>th consecutive coordinate block of
size <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and set the other coordinates to zero. Choose
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{a}=VP_{a},\,\mathbf{M}_{a}=c_{a}M_{*},\,M_{*}=e_{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}+\sum_{j=2}^{k}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>M</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mn>𝟏</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{a}=VP_{a},\,\mathbf{M}_{a}=c_{a}M_{*},\,M_{*}=e_{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}+\sum_{j=2}^{k}e_{j}e_{j}^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math>
where <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;c_{1}&lt;\cdots&lt;c_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">&lt;</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">&lt;</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>h</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;c_{1}&lt;\cdots&lt;c_{h}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Partition <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[d]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[d]</annotation></semantics></math> into <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> blocks <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> of size <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, and set
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="u_{j}=V_{:,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>V</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">:</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{j}=V_{:,j}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\leq d-s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\leq d-s</annotation></semantics></math>.
Use the probes <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i},\,(e_{1}+t_{\nu}e_{i},e_{1},e_{1}),\,(u_{j},(u_{j}+e_{b})_{b\in J})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i},\,(e_{1}+t_{\nu}e_{i},e_{1},e_{1}),\,(u_{j},(u_{j}+e_{b})_{b\in J}),</annotation></semantics></math>
for <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in[d]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in[d]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu\in[H+1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu\in[H+1]</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in[d-s]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in[d-s]</annotation></semantics></math>,
stacking the listed tokens as rows.
Their counts are exactly those specified by <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{P}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{P}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">We will repeatedly use the following elementary fact:
a nonzero polynomial of degree below <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> cannot vanish at
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> distinct points. Consequently, the matrix
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\alpha_{i}^{j-1})_{i\in I,\,j\in[q]}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>α</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\alpha_{i}^{j-1})_{i\in I,\,j\in[q]}</annotation></semantics></math> is invertible whenever
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|I|=q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>I</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|I|=q</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">We start with showing that the singleton and triple outputs constrain the value matrices.
Write <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(t)=e^{t}/(2+e^{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(t)=e^{t}/(2+e^{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Singletons determine <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=\sum_{a}\mathbf{W}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=\sum_{a}\mathbf{W}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For a fixed direction <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, subtract <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{1}^{\top}S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{1}^{\top}S</annotation></semantics></math> from a
repeated output row of the triple and divide by <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\nu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>ν</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\nu}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The result is</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text">We define:</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.3.1" class="ltx_text">Each row of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is nonzero and occupies a different coordinate
block, so its rows are independent.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">Choose the positive scales so that
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{rank}[C\ D_{a}]=h+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>rank</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0.500em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{rank}[C\ D_{a}]=h+1</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>.
Here is a real-variable justification that such scales exist.
For <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, as <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we get <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(ct)-1=-2e^{-ct}+O(e^{-2ct}),\,t\rho^{\prime}(ct)=2te^{-ct}+O(te^{-2ct})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(ct)-1=-2e^{-ct}+O(e^{-2ct}),\,t\rho^{\prime}(ct)=2te^{-ct}+O(te^{-2ct}).</annotation></semantics></math>
Suppose
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{b}\beta_{b}\rho(c_{b}t)+\gamma t\rho^{\prime}(c_{a}t)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>b</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{b}\beta_{b}\rho(c_{b}t)+\gamma t\rho^{\prime}(c_{a}t)=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Taking the limit gives <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{b}\beta_{b}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>b</mi></msub><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{b}\beta_{b}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
After subtracting this constant, consider the smallest rate
with a nonzero coefficient. Dividing by its exponential leaves
a nonzero constant or a nonzero linear function of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, plus
a term tending to zero. This is impossible.
Thus the <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h+1</annotation></semantics></math> functions are independent.
Their evaluation matrices therefore have full rank for almost
every choice of the scales, simultaneously for all <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now write <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\mathbf{M}_{a},\delta\mathbf{W}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\mathbf{M}_{a},\delta\mathbf{W}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> for first-order parameter
changes, and suppose every observed output has zero
first-order change. Then <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta S=0,\,C\delta B+\sum_{a}D_{a}\,\delta g_{a}\,b_{a}^{\top}=0." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>b</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta S=0,\,C\delta B+\sum_{a}D_{a}\,\delta g_{a}\,b_{a}^{\top}=0.</annotation></semantics></math>
Taking row combinations that cancel <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>, and multiplying by
a right inverse of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, gives <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta g_{a}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta g_{a}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>,
because <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> is not a linear combination of the columns of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\delta B=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\delta B=0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta B=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta B=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Doing this for every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p10.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\mathbf{W}_{a}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\mathbf{W}_{a}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now we show that the remaining outputs constrain the score matrices corresponding to the softmax attention.
Since <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{b}P_{a}=\mathbf{1}_{a=b}\mathbf{W}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{b}P_{a}=\mathbf{1}_{a=b}\mathbf{W}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math>, multiplying the output
on the right by <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> isolates head <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>.
For a block input <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math>, we therefore obtain <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta A_{a}\,Z\mathbf{W}_{a}=0,\,A_{a}=\operatorname{softmax}(Z\mathbf{M}_{a}Z^{\top})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>softmax</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta A_{a}\,Z\mathbf{W}_{a}=0,\,A_{a}=\operatorname{softmax}(Z\mathbf{M}_{a}Z^{\top}).</annotation></semantics></math>
Every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> selected rows of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{W}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{W}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> are independent.
Indeed, after removing nonzero row factors, their first
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> nonzero columns form the polynomial-evaluation matrix
described above. Hence the rows of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\mathbf{W}_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\mathbf{W}_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> are affinely
independent. Since also <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta A_{a}\mathbf{1}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>𝟏</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta A_{a}\mathbf{1}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, it follows
that <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta A_{a}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta A_{a}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>

<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text">Differentiating the attention log-ratios gives</span></p>
