<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.2.1" class="ltx_text">For each <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math>, the vectors <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u_{j})_{j\leq d-s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u_{j})_{j\leq d-s}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(e_{b})_{b\in J}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>J</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(e_{b})_{b\in J}</annotation></semantics></math> span <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>:
deleting rows <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> from the first <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d-s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d-s</annotation></semantics></math> columns of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math>
leaves an invertible polynomial-evaluation matrix.
Thus <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\mathbf{M}_{a}e_{b}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐌</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\mathbf{M}_{a}e_{b}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> and every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p12.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>.
We have proved that all first-order parameter changes vanish.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now we use this example to conclude the result for almost every parameter and probe tuple.
A rank-<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> matrix can locally be written as</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex98" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex98.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\begin{pmatrix}U_{11}&amp;U_{12}\\
U_{21}&amp;U_{21}U_{11}^{-1}U_{12}\end{pmatrix},\,\det U_{11}\neq 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>12</mn></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>21</mn></msub></mtd><mtd><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>21</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>U</mi><mn>11</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>12</mn></msub></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.059em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">det</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>11</mn></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{pmatrix}U_{11}&amp;U_{12}\\
U_{21}&amp;U_{21}U_{11}^{-1}U_{12}\end{pmatrix},\,\det U_{11}\neq 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.2.1" class="ltx_text">Its three displayed blocks provide <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t(2d-t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t(2d-t)</annotation></semantics></math> independent
coordinates. Thus the effective parameters with ranks
exactly <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> have <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p13.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> independent coordinates;
smaller ranks require fewer coordinates.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p14.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p14.1.1" class="ltx_text">The previous discussion shows that the matrix of first
derivatives of the outputs has rank <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> at our
chosen parameters and probes.
The same is true when differentiating with respect to the
raw factors: full-rank factors allow every first-order change
in the independent matrix coordinates.
Some square submatrix of these derivatives therefore has a
nonzero determinant. This determinant is analytic on the
connected raw parameter and probe space, so its zero set
has measure zero.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p15.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p15.1.1" class="ltx_text">Passing to the independent matrix coordinates preserves this
almost-everywhere conclusion. We note that full-rank factorizations
are locally described by these coordinates together with an
arbitrary invertible change of basis in the factors.
Fubini applied to these extra coordinates gives the assertion.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now, finally we bound the exceptional set.
Record both the probes and their outputs:</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex99" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex99.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{P},\theta)=\bigl(\mathcal{P},\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})\bigr),\,m=\dim\mathbf{P}_{0}+q." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><msub><mi>𝐏</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{P},\theta)=\bigl(\mathcal{P},\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})\bigr),\,m=\dim\mathbf{P}_{0}+q.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16.2.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> be the union of the pairs for which a
parameter matrix has smaller rank than allowed and the
remaining pairs where the matrix of first derivatives of
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math> has rank below <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p17" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p17.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p17.1.1" class="ltx_text">The smaller-rank matrices require fewer independent
coordinates. For matrices of the full allowed ranks,
the derivative condition fails on proper analytic zero sets,
by the preceding construction. Hence
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{B}\leq m-1." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{B}\leq m-1.</annotation></semantics></math>
Here we use the elementary fact that the zero set of a
nonzero analytic function on an open subset of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{m}</annotation></semantics></math>
has Hausdorff dimension at most <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p17.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m-1</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.1.1" class="ltx_text">We must also exclude parameters whose observations match
those of a point in <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>. Define <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}\coloneqq\mathcal{G}^{-1}\bigl(\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})\bigr)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}\coloneqq\mathcal{G}^{-1}\bigl(\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})\bigr).</annotation></semantics></math>
Smooth maps do not increase Hausdorff dimension. Therefore we have: <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})\leq m-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})\leq m-1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Outside <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>, select <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> coordinates of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}</annotation></semantics></math>
whose derivative matrix is invertible.
The inverse function theorem gives a smooth local inverse.
Applying this inverse to the corresponding coordinates
of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})</annotation></semantics></math> gives
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal{N}\setminus\mathcal{B})\leq\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})\leq m-1." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>∖</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">≤</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}(\mathcal{N}\setminus\mathcal{B})\leq\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})\leq m-1.</annotation></semantics></math>
A countable collection of these neighborhoods suffices.
Since <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, we conclude that <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p18.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{N}\leq m-1." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mathcal{N}\leq m-1.</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p19" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p19.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p19.1.1" class="ltx_text">The set <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> is closed: having the full allowed
matrix ranks and an invertible selected derivative matrix
are open conditions.
Thus <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math> is a countable union of compact sets.
Its continuous image <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p19.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}(\mathcal{B})</annotation></semantics></math> is likewise
such a union, so <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p19.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}</annotation></semantics></math> is measurable.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p20" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p20.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p20.1.1" class="ltx_text">If <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\mathcal{P},\theta)\notin\mathcal{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∉</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\mathcal{P},\theta)\notin\mathcal{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, every parameter with the
same observations lies outside <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p20.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The inverse function theorem therefore isolates each
matching parameter from all other matches.
There are at most countably many such isolated points.
Finally, Fubini in the independent matrix coordinates
gives the almost-everywhere conclusion in the stated order.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma11" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 11</span></span><span id="Thmlemma11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Prefixes are generically locally invertible)<span id="Thmlemma11.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each fixed length <math id="Thmlemma11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> and prefix depth <math id="Thmlemma11.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>, the input
Jacobian of <math id="Thmlemma11.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\ell,n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\ell,n}</annotation></semantics></math> is nonsingular almost everywhere in
the raw prefix parameters and input. Consequently, for almost
every prefix, its image contains a nonempty open set.</span></p>
</div>
</div>

for sufficiently small <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p21.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
The full input Jacobian is block triangular with invertible
diagonal blocks <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p21.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Df_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Df_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p21.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d-1</annotation></semantics></math> copies of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p21.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>ε</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p22" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p22.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p22.1.1" class="ltx_text">The output first coordinates remain distinct: the function
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q\mapsto\sum_{j}z_{j}e^{\varepsilon qz_{j}}/\sum_{j}e^{\varepsilon qz_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo rspace="0.111em" stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q\mapsto\sum_{j}z_{j}e^{\varepsilon qz_{j}}/\sum_{j}e^{\varepsilon qz_{j}}</annotation></semantics></math>
has derivative <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p22.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math> times a positive weighted variance.
We can therefore repeat the construction through each layer.
For <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p22.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=1</annotation></semantics></math> the witness is the identity.
Each prefix determinant is consequently a nonzero analytic
function. Its zero set is null; Fubini and the inverse function
theorem give the conclusion.
∎</span></p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The geometric strengthening.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The following standard result is the only additional external
ingredient used to obtain the open-probes and closed-exception
claims. We state it explicitly rather than treating those
claims as consequences of analyticity.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem12" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 12</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Real-exponential geometry; external input)<span id="Thmtheorem12.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem12.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Thmtheorem12.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem12.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Call a set <em id="Thmtheorem12.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">definable</em> if it can be described by a finite
formula using real constants, arithmetic, exponentials,
equalities, inequalities and quantifiers over real variables.
Such sets have integer Hausdorff dimension, satisfy</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex103" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex103.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\overline{A}=\dim_{\mathrm{H}}A,\,A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}\text{ is null}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \dim_{\mathrm{H}}A&lt;m," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mi>A</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic"> is null</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0.778em" rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><mi>H</mi></msub><mi>A</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\overline{A}=\dim_{\mathrm{H}}A,\,A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}\text{ is null}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \dim_{\mathrm{H}}A&lt;m,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Thmtheorem12.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem12.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">and, for a definable family <math id="Thmtheorem12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{s}\times\mathbb{R}^{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>s</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>D</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{s}\times\mathbb{R}^{D}</annotation></semantics></math>,
each set <math id="Thmtheorem12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{u:\dim_{\mathrm{H}}B_{u}=j\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.111em" rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></msub><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{u:\dim_{\mathrm{H}}B_{u}=j\}</annotation></semantics></math> is definable.
Here <math id="Thmtheorem12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dim\varnothing=-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">dim</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dim\varnothing=-\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This is a consequence of Wilkie’s o-minimality theorem for
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}_{\exp}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>exp</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}_{\exp}</annotation></semantics></math> and its dimension theory
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wilkie, 2009</a>)</cite>;
we do not reprove that foundational theorem.</p>
</div>

full-rank stratum. Pulling back the exceptional set in

For almost every first batch and target, each layer has only
countably many consistent effective candidates. This includes
every matching competitor: its hidden transcript fixes the
same layer inputs as those observed from the target.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px4.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">Finally we show that the failure set is measurable.
At each layer, give the competitor’s heads positive signs and
the target’s heads negative signs. Canonical agreement means that these
signed heads can be partitioned into groups with equal score
matrices and zero signed value sums. There are finitely many
partitions, each imposing polynomial equalities. Canonical
agreement is therefore closed.
The incidence set of matching transcripts but canonical
disagreement is closed intersected with open, hence a countable
union of compact sets. Its projection</span></p>

<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multilayer MHA reconstruction from a fixed set of probes</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The observations already supply each layer’s training inputs:
they are the preceding <em id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">target</em> states, not states generated
by the reconstructed prefix. Each layer can consequently be
fitted independently. Define its cached-data loss by</p>

<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Correctness and scope.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each feasibility problem has a solution, the true layer.
Induction over <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> shows that the returned stack reproduces
every recorded state. Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem13" title="Theorem 13 (Structured probing for softmax attention). ‣ The geometric strengthening. ‣ B.4 Function-level identification of multi-head attention ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> therefore gives
the all-length conclusion.
In numerical implementations it is replaced by layerwise
least-squares optimization. It should be mentioned that neither its global convergence nor
an OOD error bound from a nonzero residual follows from the theorem. The theorem provides a guarantee, the implementation requires implementing a solver or independently fitting the layers.
No head alignment <em id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">between layers</em> is required.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The special case of one layer:</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The above statement in Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem13" title="Theorem 13 (Structured probing for softmax attention). ‣ The geometric strengthening. ‣ B.4 Function-level identification of multi-head attention ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> discusses identification of generic targets from probes in the multilayer case. However, we show in the following lemma that for a single layer, we can <em id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">exactly identify every target</em> at a function level.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmlemma12" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmlemma12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 12</span></span><span id="Thmlemma12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(One layer: every target from fixed probes)<span id="Thmlemma12.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmlemma12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmlemma12.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmlemma12.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmlemma12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmlemma12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=4dh+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=4dh+1</annotation></semantics></math>. There exist an integer <math id="Thmlemma12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{*}=n_{*}(d,h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{*}=n_{*}(d,h)</annotation></semantics></math>
and a fixed probe set <math id="Thmlemma12.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\in(\mathbb{R}^{n_{*}\times d})^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\in(\mathbb{R}^{n_{*}\times d})^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> such that,
simultaneously for all <math id="Thmlemma12.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{1},\theta_{2}\in\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{1},\theta_{2}\in\Theta</annotation></semantics></math>, we have:</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx61" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex112.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta_{1};\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta_{2};\mathcal{P})\,\iff\,\left[F_{n}(\cdot;\theta_{1})\equiv F_{n}(\cdot;\theta_{2})\text{ for every }n\geq 1\right]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">final</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>;</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">final</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>;</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.448em" stretchy="false">⇔</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≡</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic"> for every </mtext><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta_{1};\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta_{2};\mathcal{P})\,\iff\,\left[F_{n}(\cdot;\theta_{1})\equiv F_{n}(\cdot;\theta_{2})\text{ for every }n\geq 1\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Put <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=(d-1)(2h-1)+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=(d-1)(2h-1)+1</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}=(1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1})^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}=(1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1})^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=1,\ldots,K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=1,\ldots,K</annotation></semantics></math>,
and let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math> contain the distinct vectors among
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0,e_{1},\ldots,e_{d},q_{1},\ldots,q_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0,e_{1},\ldots,e_{d},q_{1},\ldots,q_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For positive integer multiplicities <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=(m_{x})_{x\in\mathcal{D}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=(m_{x})_{x\in\mathcal{D}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X(m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X(m)</annotation></semantics></math> contain <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{x}</annotation></semantics></math> copies of each <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.
At a copy of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, output coordinate <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> equals</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Clearing the positive denominators of
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(m;\xi)-R(m;\xi^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(m;\xi)-R(m;\xi^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> gives a polynomial <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(m;\xi,\xi^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(m;\xi,\xi^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>,
since every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math> has nonnegative integer coordinates.
The Finite Witness Theorem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amir et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, applied to the <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4dh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4dh</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional pair <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\xi,\xi^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\xi,\xi^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>, implies that almost every choice of <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=4dh+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=4dh+1</annotation></semantics></math> generic positive multiplicity vectors detects every nonzero discrepancy.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">The bad witness set is semialgebraic:
writing <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P=\sum_{\alpha}c_{\alpha}(\xi,\xi^{\prime})m^{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>α</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mi>α</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P=\sum_{\alpha}c_{\alpha}(\xi,\xi^{\prime})m^{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>, it is the
projection of the set defined by <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{\alpha}c_{\alpha}^{2}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>α</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{\alpha}c_{\alpha}^{2}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(m^{(j)};\xi,\xi^{\prime})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ξ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(m^{(j)};\xi,\xi^{\prime})=0</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>.
Its nullity implies that its closure has empty interior.
We choose a good rational tuple. Since
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(\lambda m;\xi)=R(m;\xi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(\lambda m;\xi)=R(m;\xi)</annotation></semantics></math>, normalize each vector to sum one
and clear all denominators by a common integer. This gives
positive integer multiplicities of a common sum <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The resulting probe set works for every row and coordinate, because
their parameters all belong to <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ξ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Xi</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Suppose two layers agree on this set of probes. Let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{1},\ldots,B_{J}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>J</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{1},\ldots,B_{J}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J\leq 2h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J\leq 2h</annotation></semantics></math>, be their distinct score matrices, and let <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>
be the difference of their summed value matrices at <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, some <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{\top}B_{j}\neq q_{t}^{\top}B_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{\top}B_{j}\neq q_{t}^{\top}B_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\neq j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\neq j</annotation></semantics></math>:
any <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> moment-curve vectors are independent, so each proper
subspace <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{q:q^{\top}(B_{j}-B_{l})=0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{q:q^{\top}(B_{j}-B_{l})=0\}</annotation></semantics></math> contains at most <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d-1</annotation></semantics></math>
of them, fewer than <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> altogether.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix this <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}=q_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}=q_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and a coordinate <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>. The witness property gives</span></p>

movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>x</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{l=1}^{J}\frac{A_{l}(m)}{D_{l}(m)}\equiv 0,\,D_{l}=\sum_{x}m_{x}e^{x_{0}^{\top}B_{l}x},\,A_{l}=\sum_{x}m_{x}e^{x_{0}^{\top}B_{l}x}x^{\top}\Delta_{l}e_{c}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Each denominator has coefficient one at <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, and its
coefficients at <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{e_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{e_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> determine <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}^{\top}B_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}^{\top}B_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>.
After merging equal denominators, <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> is a distinct linear
factor. Clearing denominators shows that this prime factor
divides <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{j}=\lambda D_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{j}=\lambda D_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The coefficient at <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=0</annotation></semantics></math>; the coefficients
at <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{e_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{e_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> then give <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Delta_{j})_{ic}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Delta_{j})_{ic}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus all <math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px7.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{j}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{j}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, proving
functional agreement at every length.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5 </span>Learning Functionals and Operators from Probes</h3>

<div id="A2.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first prove a common approximation lemma. We then give formal
versions of Theorems <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem 6 (Universality of probe-based learning). ‣ 6 Universality of probe-based learning ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>
and <a href="#Thmtheorem7" title="Theorem 7 (Universality of HiddenProbe). ‣ 6 Universality of probe-based learning ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, in that order.
All function spaces below carry the uniform norm. Matrix inputs,
outputs, and observations are identified with vectors by listing
their entries in a fixed order. All MLP readouts have biases,
an affine output layer, and a fixed continuous, non-polynomial
hidden activation <math id="A2.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

K}\sup_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\|\mathcal{T}(f_{\theta})(y)-\psi(R(\theta),y)\|_{2}&lt;\epsilon.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Uniform continuity of <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}\times K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}\times K</annotation></semantics></math> implies continuity
of the realization map <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\real:K\to C(\mathcal{X},\mathbb{R}^{m}),\,\real(\theta)=f_{\theta}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\real:K\to C(\mathcal{X},\mathbb{R}^{m}),\,\real(\theta)=f_{\theta},</annotation></semantics></math>
in the uniform norm. Thus <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{F}_{K}=\real(K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{F}_{K}=\real(K)</annotation></semantics></math> is compact.
Put <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=R(K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=R(K)</annotation></semantics></math> and define <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(R(\theta))=f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(R(\theta))=f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Separation makes <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> well defined. For every closed
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

Hence <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">The map <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda\circ g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda\circ g</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on the compact set <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>.
The universal approximation theorem
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Leshno et al. (1993)</a></cite> gives an MLP <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sup_{s\in S}\|\Lambda(g(s))-\phi(s)\|_{2}&lt;\epsilon." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>sup</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sup_{s\in S}\|\Lambda(g(s))-\phi(s)\|_{2}&lt;\epsilon.</annotation></semantics></math>
Substituting <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s=R(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=R(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> proves the functional conclusion.
The compact-set, vector-valued form follows by applying the
Tietze extension theorem and the scalar approximation theorem
coordinatewise.</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The following Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem15" title="Theorem 15 (Approximation from final-output probes). ‣ Final-output observations. ‣ B.5 Learning Functionals and Operators from Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> is the formal version of
Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem 6 (Universality of probe-based learning). ‣ 6 Universality of probe-based learning ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmtheorem15" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 15</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Approximation from final-output probes)<span id="Thmtheorem15.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmtheorem15.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="Thmtheorem15.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmtheorem15.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmtheorem15.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{q}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{q}\to\mathbb{R}^{m}</annotation></semantics></math> be real analytic,
let <math id="Thmtheorem15.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> be compact with nonempty interior,
and let <math id="Thmtheorem15.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{q}</annotation></semantics></math> be compact.
For every <math id="Thmtheorem15.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\geq 2q+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\geq 2q+1</annotation></semantics></math>, and for almost every
<math id="Thmtheorem15.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\cdots,p_{N})\in\mathcal{X}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>N</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\cdots,p_{N})\in\mathcal{X}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the map</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx69" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is globally analytic, we may apply
Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Unique reconstruction from finite samples). ‣ 2 Identifying Analytic Neural Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> on sufficiently large input and
parameter balls containing <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta</annotation></semantics></math> in their
interiors. Restricting the parameters to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta</annotation></semantics></math> and
intersecting the exceptional probe set with <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}^{2q+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}^{2q+1}</annotation></semantics></math>
gives a Lebesgue-null <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}_{0}\subseteq\mathcal{X}^{2q+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}_{0}\subseteq\mathcal{X}^{2q+1}</annotation></semantics></math> outside
which final-output observations separate all represented functions.
For <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N&gt;2q+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N&gt;2q+1</annotation></semantics></math>, take
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{N}_{0}\times\mathcal{X}^{N-2q-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{N}_{0}\times\mathcal{X}^{N-2q-1}</annotation></semantics></math>;
for <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=2q+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=2q+1</annotation></semantics></math>, take <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{N}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}=\mathcal{N}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Fix <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\notin\mathcal{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∉</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\notin\mathcal{N}</annotation></semantics></math>. The map <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(\theta)\coloneqq\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≔</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(\theta)\coloneqq\Psi_{\text{final}}(\theta,\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>
is continuous and separates functions on <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma13" title="Lemma 13 (Separation implies universal approximation). ‣ Separation and approximation. ‣ B.5 Learning Functionals and Operators from Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, with <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=\Theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=\Theta</annotation></semantics></math>,
gives both approximation conclusions and a continuous map
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g:R(\Theta)\to\mathcal{F}_{\Theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g:R(\Theta)\to\mathcal{F}_{\Theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Separation makes <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> one-to-one, and
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(T_{\mathcal{P}}(f_{\theta}))=f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(T_{\mathcal{P}}(f_{\theta}))=f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=T_{\mathcal{P}}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=T_{\mathcal{P}}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Also,</span></p>

<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Hidden-layer observations.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The following Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem16" title="Theorem 16 (Approximation from hidden-layer probes). ‣ Hidden-layer observations. ‣ B.5 Learning Functionals and Operators from Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> is the formal version of
Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem7" title="Theorem 7 (Universality of HiddenProbe). ‣ 6 Universality of probe-based learning ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.
We retain the complete final probe responses in their coordinate
order, but discard the ordering of the hidden neurons or channels.
For MLPs and MHA stacks, respectively, define</p>
<table id="A2.EGx72" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A2.Ex124"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

Let <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math> be the
multiset of these vectors, including repetitions

<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{i}=d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{i}=d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=N</annotation></semantics></math> for MLPs and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{i}=d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{i}=d</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=\sum_{j}n_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=\sum_{j}n_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> for MHA.</p>
