<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> are MLPs satisfying the preceding
activation and bias assumptions, with unrestricted hidden
widths and encoder output dimension.
The same <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varphi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>φ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varphi</annotation></semantics></math> is used for every hidden channel and layer.
The final responses <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{final}}(\cdot,\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{final}}(\cdot,\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> retain their coordinate order.
For operators, the prediction MLP additionally receives
the query input.</p>
</div>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmtheorem16.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 16</span></span><span id="Thmtheorem16.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Approximation from hidden-layer probes)<span id="Thmtheorem16.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{U}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}\in\mathcal{U}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For MLPs, we define</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">By Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma2" title="Lemma 2. ‣ When the activation is also injective and non polynomial: ‣ B.1 Identification of Analytic MLPs from Hidden Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, the displayed
product is a nonzero real-analytic function of <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Its zero set is closed and has Hausdorff dimension at most
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-1</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{0}\notin E_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{0}\notin E_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>, equality of the ordered
observations with any raw competitor gives, by injectivity,
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(B_{i}-B_{i}^{0})\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})=0,\,0\leq i&lt;L." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐗</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(B_{i}-B_{i}^{0})\overline{\mathbf{X}}_{i}^{\theta_{0}}(\mathcal{P})=0,\,0\leq i&lt;L.</annotation></semantics></math>
Full row rank gives <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{i}=B_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{i}=B_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>.
For an affine output layer, its equality follows directly
without inverting an activation.
For attention, use <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> from Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem13" title="Theorem 13 (Structured probing for softmax attention). ‣ The geometric strengthening. ‣ B.4 Function-level identification of multi-head attention ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>.
That theorem also identifies every target outside <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math>
against every raw competitor, at every sequence length.</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now fix compact <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K\subseteq\Theta\setminus E_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mo>∖</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K\subseteq\Theta\setminus E_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta,\theta_{0}\in K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta,\theta_{0}\in K</annotation></semantics></math> with
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathcal{P}}(\theta)=R_{\mathcal{P}}(\theta_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathcal{P}}(\theta)=R_{\mathcal{P}}(\theta_{0})</annotation></semantics></math>.

Again, <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta^{\prime},\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta^{\prime},\mathcal{P})=\Psi_{\text{all}}(\theta_{0},\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta^{\prime}}=f_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta^{\prime}}=f_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The all-competitor identification established above implies
<math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}=f_{\theta_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}=f_{\theta_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> in either case.
It is unnecessary that <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> belong to <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">The map <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous, since its coordinates are
polynomials in finitely many continuous observations.
The realization is jointly continuous on the chosen compact
input domain and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>. Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma13" title="Lemma 13 (Separation implies universal approximation). ‣ Separation and approximation. ‣ B.5 Learning Functionals and Operators from Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>
therefore gives <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\mathcal{P}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\mathcal{P}}</annotation></semantics></math> and continuous functional and operator
readouts on <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathcal{P}}(K)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathcal{P}}(K)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathcal{P}}(K)\times\mathcal{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathcal{P}}(K)\times\mathcal{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>.
It remains to realize their approximations by the specified
architectures.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p9.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>, Set Transformer universality
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. (2019)</a></cite>, with sufficient capacity and output
dimension, approximates each layer’s continuous invariant
map <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{r_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{r_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The final MLP approximates the resulting
continuous readout.</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>, the case <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L=1</annotation></semantics></math> follows directly from
Lemma <a href="#Thmlemma13" title="Lemma 13 (Separation implies universal approximation). ‣ Separation and approximation. ‣ B.5 Learning Functionals and Operators from Probes ‣ Appendix B Proof of Technical results ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, since there are
no hidden trajectories. Suppose <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, and define</span></p>
<table id="A2.EGx81" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.6.1" class="ltx_text">Replacing <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho(z)</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px3.p10.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi(z,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi(z,y)</annotation></semantics></math> and taking the

The independence assertions follow from the identification
theorems.
∎</span></p>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Architectural details of <span id="A3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> and <span id="A3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span></h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We describe the architectures and training procedures of
<span id="A3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> for MLPs and <span id="A3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> for Transformers in separate subsections.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span><span id="A3.SS1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> for MLPs</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We describe the architectures used for INR classification
and Model Zoo regression tasks.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.1.1 </span>INR Classification</h4>

<section id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Target networks and learned probes.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For INR classification, each target is a SIREN with sine activations. We use <math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=128</annotation></semantics></math> learned coordinate probes. Each probe has a
trainable code <math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta_{q}\in\mathbb{R}^{32}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>32</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta_{q}\in\mathbb{R}^{32}</annotation></semantics></math>, initialized from
<math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{N}(0,I_{32})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mn>32</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{N}(0,I_{32})</annotation></semantics></math>. Two shared affine maps generate
the coordinates:</p>
<table id="A3.EGx86" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex145"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex145.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle u_{q}=\tanh\bigl(A_{2}(A_{1}\zeta_{q}+b_{1})+b_{2}\bigr)\in(-1,1)^{2},\qquad A_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{32\times 32},\quad A_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 32}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>tanh</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ζ</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle u_{q}=\tanh\bigl(A_{2}(A_{1}\zeta_{q}+b_{1})+b_{2}\bigr)\in(-1,1)^{2},\qquad A_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{32\times 32},\quad A_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 32}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">There is no activation between the affine maps.
The same ordered probe bank is presented to every target;
generation is not conditioned on the target’s weights
or responses.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Observed responses and neuron trajectories.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For INR classification, during one forward pass, we record the two hidden
layer responses <math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{i}^{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 32}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{i}^{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 32}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,2</annotation></semantics></math>, and final outputs <math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O^{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>O</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O^{\theta}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times 3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each hidden neuron, we collect its responses across
the complete bank:</p>
<table id="A3.EGx87" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex146"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex146.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle v_{x}^{i,c}(\theta)=\bigl([X_{i}^{\theta}]_{q,c}\bigr)_{n=1}^{N}\in\mathbb{R}^{128},\qquad i\in\{1,2\},\quad c\in[32]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>v</mi><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>128</mn></msup></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>32</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle v_{x}^{i,c}(\theta)=\bigl([X_{i}^{\theta}]_{q,c}\bigr)_{n=1}^{N}\in\mathbb{R}^{128},\qquad i\in\{1,2\},\quad c\in[32].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We design features by concatenating the activations with global features: mean, standard deviation, maximum,
minimum. Denoting these statistics by
<math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s(v)</annotation></semantics></math>, the resulting feature vector is <math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi(v)=[v;s(v)]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>;</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi(v)=[v;s(v)].</annotation></semantics></math>
No normalization is applied before the token projection.
Probe order is retained within every trajectory.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Neuron tokens and joint readout.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A shared affine map projects every neuron feature to
<math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d_{e}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and a learned embedding <math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> identifies its
hidden layer:</p>
<table id="A3.EGx88" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex147"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex147.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle t_{i,c}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle t_{i,c}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex147.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=A\chi\bigl(v_{x}^{i,c}(\theta)\bigr)+a+e_{i}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>v</mi><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=A\chi\bigl(v_{x}^{i,c}(\theta)\bigr)+a+e_{i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A3.Ex148"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex148.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle t_{\mathrm{out}}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mi>out</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle t_{\mathrm{out}}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex148.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=A_{\mathrm{out}}\operatorname{vec}(O^{\theta})+a_{\mathrm{out}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>out</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>vec</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>O</mi><mi>θ</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>out</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=A_{\mathrm{out}}\operatorname{vec}(O^{\theta})+a_{\mathrm{out}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">One joint Transformer processes all tokens.
We use three blocks: each block has eight attention heads,
feedforward, ReLU, dropout <math id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> and
LayerNorm before its attention and feedforward sublayers.
There is no final LayerNorm after the last block.
An MLP maps the final CLS token to class logits.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">There are no neuron-index embeddings or sequence
positional encodings. At evaluation, when dropout is
disabled, permuting the neurons within a hidden layer
only permutes their tokens and leaves the prediction
unchanged. Probe order, in contrast, is retained in both
the trajectories and final-output vector.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relation to the theory.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS1.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The neuron tokens preserve correspondence across probes,
as in the theoretical trajectory representation.
The implementation processes the layers jointly rather
than using separate layerwise set encoders; layer
embeddings retain their identities. It also observes
preactivations, from which the theoretical postactivation
responses can be computed.
Sine is analytic but not injective, so the
parameter-identification theorem stated for injective
activations does not apply directly to these targets.
The learned probes and finite-width token projections
are not assumed to satisfy exact separation conditions.
The universality results concern capacity-growing
architecture families under their stated assumptions,
not every fixed-width encoder or trained parameter choice.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.1.2 </span><span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> for CNN-zoo accuracy regression</h4>

<section id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Target networks and learned probes</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The regression targets are image-classification CNNs.
The grayscale zoos use three convolutional layers with
channels <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\to 16\to 16\to 16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>16</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\to 16\to 16\to 16</annotation></semantics></math>, kernel size <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> and stride
<math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, followed by global average pooling and a ten-output
affine classifier. The Wild Park zoo contains targets
with different depths, channel counts, convolutional
settings and activations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Here, we use <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=128</annotation></semantics></math> learned image probes. Each probe is generated from a trainable code in <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{32\times 1\times 1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{32\times 1\times 1}</annotation></semantics></math> and has the appropriate image dimensions. A final <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>tanh</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh</annotation></semantics></math> bounds the image values to <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(-1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>. The same learned probe bank is used for every target network. The output and hidden-response branches described below share this probe bank and the same target forward pass. We follow a protocol similar to that of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kahana et al. (2025)</a></cite> for learning probes in classification and regression tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Hidden aggregation and Prediction</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The regressor stacks the probes’ output at each channel and then pools the channels within each layer. Like in the case of INR classification, we also use additional global statistics like channelwise means, maxima, standard deviation etc
over probes to design extra features to aggregate all the information from hidden layers.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">One self-attention block mixes the layer vectors using
a learned relative-layer distance bias, followed by a
residual pre-LayerNorm feedforward block with GELU.
A final attention pool over layers, funal output and a projection
give <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{H}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>H</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>z</mi></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{H}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{z}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The attention projections in this aggregation have
inner dimension <math id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>; large hidden-branch projections
use factorized weights to reduce the number of parameters, and match the parameter count with that of ProbeGen.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The predictor is an MLP that taken in the hidden combined representation and gives a scalar that predicts the accuracy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relation to the theory</h5>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The regressor follows the shared-probe principle and
uses hidden responses without additional target-network
queries. Its channel pooling respects channel
permutations. It is an empirical adaptation of hidden
probing in the context of CNN Model Zoo.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span><span id="A3.SS2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> for Transformers</h3>

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Details on the learned probes.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For MNIST, we use <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=256</annotation></semantics></math> probes divided into two families.
The first contains <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">192</annotation></semantics></math> learned sequences, each consisting
of <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math> token vectors in <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{32}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>32</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{32}</annotation></semantics></math>. The remaining
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> probes are learned <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28\times 28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>28</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28\times 28</annotation></semantics></math> images.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each encoder probe is parameterized by independently learned
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional token codes. Each image is parameterized by
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="49" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>49</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">49</annotation></semantics></math> learned <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>16</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional codes, corresponding to its
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4\times 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times 4</annotation></semantics></math> patches. Within each route, a shared residual
two-layer MLP transforms these codes: <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G(z)=z+W_{2}\operatorname{GELU}(W_{1}z+b_{1})+b_{2}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>GELU</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G(z)=z+W_{2}\operatorname{GELU}(W_{1}z+b_{1})+b_{2}.</annotation></semantics></math>
The transformed image patches are assembled into a
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="28\times 28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>28</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">28\times 28</annotation></semantics></math> image.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The same learned bank is presented to every target:
generation is not conditioned on the target’s weights
or its responses.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Observed responses and channel trajectories.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For MNIST and AGNews datasets, the Transformers have two blocks.
For every probe, we record the outputs of the target’s two
transformer blocks, its final normalized token states,
and its classifier logits. Denote the three hidden layers
by <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X_{\mathrm{norm}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>norm</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X_{\mathrm{norm}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Each hidden layer has <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> channels, and each probe produces
a <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional logit vector.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each layer <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,2,\mathrm{norm}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>norm</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,2,\mathrm{norm}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and channel
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in[32]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>32</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in[32]</annotation></semantics></math>, we concatenate that channel’s responses across
all probes and token positions:</p>
<table id="A3.Ex149" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex149.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v^{i,c}(\theta)=\left([X_{i}(P_{j};\theta)]_{t,c}\right)_{j\in[N],\,t\in[n_{j}]}\in\mathbb{R}^{T},\," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v^{i,c}(\theta)=\left([X_{i}(P_{j};\theta)]_{t,c}\right)_{j\in[N],\,t\in[n_{j}]}\in\mathbb{R}^{T},\,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The concatenation uses a fixed order: encoder probes first,
then image probes, with token positions kept in order
within each probe. Consequently, each channel is represented
by its responses to the complete bank.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Encoding and combining channel features.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One shared trajectory encoder <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> is applied independently
to every channel in all three blocks: <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u^{i,c}=E(v^{i,c})\in\mathbb{R}^{192}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>192</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^{i,c}=E(v^{i,c})\in\mathbb{R}^{192}.</annotation></semantics></math>
The encoder consists of
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Linear}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Linear</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Linear}</annotation></semantics></math>, GELU,
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Linear}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Linear</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Linear}</annotation></semantics></math>, and LayerNorm.
It produces <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> feature vectors for each view; it does
not pool across channels.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We then combine each block-2 feature with the
final-normalized feature of the same channel:
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{u}^{2,c}=\operatorname{Fuse}\left([u^{2,c};u^{\mathrm{norm},c}]\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{192}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>u</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Fuse</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup><mo>;</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>norm</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>192</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{u}^{2,c}=\operatorname{Fuse}\left([u^{2,c};u^{\mathrm{norm},c}]\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{192}.</annotation></semantics></math> This is concatenated with the <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> block-1 features, giving
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>64</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">64</annotation></semantics></math> hidden-response tokens in total.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Joint readout and pooling.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each probe’s classifier logits are projected from
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{10}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>10</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{10}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{192}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>192</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{192}</annotation></semantics></math>. Together with a learned CLS token, the readout input
contains <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1+32+32+256=321" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>321</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1+32+32+256=321</annotation></semantics></math> tokens of dimension <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="192" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>192</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">192</annotation></semantics></math>. Two pre-Layernorm Transformer
blocks process these tokens jointly, a final LayerNorm is applied to their
outputs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Write the resulting tokens as
<math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{\mathrm{CLS}},z_{1},\ldots,z_{320}\in\mathbb{R}^{192}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>CLS</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mn>320</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>192</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{\mathrm{CLS}},z_{1},\ldots,z_{320}\in\mathbb{R}^{192}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We form</p>
<table id="A3.Ex150" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex150.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\theta}=\left[z_{\mathrm{CLS}};\frac{1}{320}\sum_{a=1}^{320}z_{a};\max_{a\in[320]}z_{a}\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{576}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>CLS</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>320</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>320</mn></munderover><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>;</mo><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>320</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>576</mn></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\theta}=\left[z_{\mathrm{CLS}};\frac{1}{320}\sum_{a=1}^{320}z_{a};\max_{a\in[320]}z_{a}\right]\in\mathbb{R}^{576},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where the maximum is coordinatewise.
Thus, mean and maximum pooling act jointly over all
non-CLS tokens, including the logit tokens, rather than
separately within each layer.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">A prediction head with dimensions <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="576\to 192\to 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>576</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>192</mn><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">576\to 192\to 1</annotation></semantics></math> and
a GELU activation maps <math id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> to standardized
accuracy. The predictor receives only the recorded responses and
fixed semantic identifiers, not target weights, target
identities, or generated probe coordinates.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Relation to the theory.</h5>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The theoretical constructions motivate a shared bank
with different sequence lengths and the use of intermediate
responses. The experiments apply these principles to
complete transformer classifiers containing feedforward
and normalization layers. They do not assume that the
learned probes satisfy the exact reconstruction conditions
or identify the target function. Likewise, the universality
results concern capacity-growing architecture families,
not a guarantee for this particular finite-width
configuration or its learned parameters.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Experimental details</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Function-level reconstruction on synthetic neural networks</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To illustrate the benefits of hidden activations, we study function-level reconstruction of frozen neural networks from a limited number of input probes. We compare <em id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">output-only regression</em>, which observes only the final network outputs, with <em id="A4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">intermediate-layer regression</em>, which independently fits each layer using observed teacher activations as its inputs and targets. Our goal is to examine how well each approach reconstructs the target function, both between the observed probes and outside the training interval.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Common Setup</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider function-level reconstruction of MLPs with different activations and stacks of MHA blocks, using either final outputs alone or complete hidden-layer observations. Let <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\theta}\coloneqq(\theta_{1},\ldots,\theta_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>≔</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\theta}\coloneqq(\theta_{1},\ldots,\theta_{L})</annotation></semantics></math> denote the parameters of a sequential model
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="f_{\bm{\theta}}=f_{\theta_{L}}\circ\cdots\circ f_{\theta_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mo lspace="0.055em" rspace="0.055em">⋯</mo><mo rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>f</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\bm{\theta}}=f_{\theta_{L}}\circ\cdots\circ f_{\theta_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Given a set of probes <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}=(p_{1},\ldots,p_{N})</annotation></semantics></math>, we observe either the final outputs <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{final}}(\bm{\theta},\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{final}}(\bm{\theta},\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math> or the complete hidden-layer observations <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}(\bm{\theta},\mathcal{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}(\bm{\theta},\mathcal{P})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For the output-only case we do MSE regression to interpolate on the probes. If <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\hat{\bm{\theta}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\hat{\bm{\theta}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the “student” network trying to reconstruct the “teacher” network, we minimize the following losses: (i) For learning from <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{final}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{final}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we minimize <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\min_{\hat{\bm{\theta}}}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|f_{\hat{\bm{\theta}}}(p_{i})-f_{{\bm{\theta}}}(p_{i})\|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em">⁡</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>𝜽</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>𝜽</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{\hat{\bm{\theta}}}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|f_{\hat{\bm{\theta}}}(p_{i})-f_{{\bm{\theta}}}(p_{i})\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (ii) For learning from <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we fit sum of MSE on each of the <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> layers, given by <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{\ell}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|f_{\hat{\theta_{\ell}}}(X^{\ell-1}_{i})-X^{\ell}_{i}\|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mover accent="true"><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{\ell}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|f_{\hat{\theta_{\ell}}}(X^{\ell-1}_{i})-X^{\ell}_{i}\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="X^{\ell}_{i}\coloneqq f_{\theta_{\ell}}\circ\cdots\circ f_{\theta_{1}}(p_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo>≔</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mo lspace="0.055em" rspace="0.055em">⋯</mo><mo rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X^{\ell}_{i}\coloneqq f_{\theta_{\ell}}\circ\cdots\circ f_{\theta_{1}}(p_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{X^{\ell}_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{X^{\ell}_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> are the observed outputs from the <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>-th layer. Here we fit each hidden layer independently but simultaneously using MSE regression.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Analytic MLP:</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We used a neural network with <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tanh" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>tanh</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tanh</annotation></semantics></math> activation of widths <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1,4,4,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1,4,4,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the training interval was <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, and the evaluation
interval is <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-3,3]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-3,3]</annotation></semantics></math>. As shown in <a href="#A4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Analytic MLP: ‣ D.1 Function-level reconstruction on synthetic neural networks ‣ Appendix D Experimental details ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 4</span></a>, access to the hidden activations enables essentially exact reconstruction once sufficiently many observations are available, whereas reconstruction from final outputs alone improves much more gradually and retains a substantially larger error even as the number of observed samples increases.</p>
</div>

<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">ReLU MLP:</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As in the analytic activation case, Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 4 (semi-formal-PAC identification of ReLU networks). ‣ 3.2 Identifying ReLU Networks from Probe evaluations ‣ 3 Probing MLPs ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> suggests that hidden activations can reduce the number of probes necessary to (almost) identify a ReLU network. We take a target ReLU network with 2 hidden layers, width 4 and weights that represent a member of the “sawtooth” function class, having a large number of breakpoints. As discussed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hanin and Rolnick (2019)</a></cite>, such a large number of breakpoints is atypical. This makes the target a challenging example for reconstruction from final outputs alone using MSE regression from random initialization. This matches the observation: we can’t reconstruct the target with just the final output. But with hidden activations, we can reconstruct the target almost exactly with far fewer probes. The same is also reflected in the out-of-distribution MSE plots</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F5" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A4.F5.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2609.33901v2/Synthetic/relu_output.png" id="A4.F5.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/285;" width="548" height="285" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">(a) </span>OOD MSE from <math id="A4.F5.sf1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{final}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{final}}</annotation></semantics></math></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A4.F5.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2609.33901v2/Synthetic/relu_all.png" id="A4.F5.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/295;" width="548" height="295" alt="Refer to caption">

</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">

</figure>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi Head Attention Stack</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Here, we want to reconstruct an MHA stack. We randomly initialize a two-layer multi-head attention network with input width <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=4</annotation></semantics></math>, two heads per layer
and query/key and value widths <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=r=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=r=2</annotation></semantics></math> (bias-free softmax attention, without residual connections, normalization or feed-forward blocks). We sample four single-token inputs
followed by generic three-token inputs, and a budget of <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> probes uses the first <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> of them, for
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> from 5 to 40. We fit the “student” MHA block jointly using <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{final}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{final}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and each layer independently using <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{all}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{all}}</annotation></semantics></math>, both using MSE regression as described above.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2609.33901v2/paper_plots/MHA_final.png" id="A4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:274/158;" width="274" height="158" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span>Reconstruction of MHA Stack from <math id="A4.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi_{\text{final}},\Psi_{\text{all}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mtext>all</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi_{\text{final}},\Psi_{\text{all}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in <a href="#A4.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Multi Head Attention Stack ‣ D.1 Function-level reconstruction on synthetic neural networks ‣ Appendix D Experimental details ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 6</span></a>, access to the hidden
activations enables essentially exact reconstruction from as few as nine probes, below the <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=21</annotation></semantics></math> probes that Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 5 (Structured probing for softmax attention). ‣ 4 Identifying Multi-Head Attention from Probes ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> predicts, whereas reconstruction from final outputs alone becomes exact only at about 31 probes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Together, these three experiments suggest that hidden activations enable more accurate function reconstruction with fewer probes than final outputs alone. This observation is consistent with our empirical results on neural functional learning, where <span id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>, which uses hidden activations, outperforms ProbeGen, which relies only on final outputs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Full INR Classification Comparison</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ D.2 Full INR Classification Comparison ‣ Appendix D Experimental details ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> provides an extended comparison on the INR classification benchmarks, including both recent weight-space methods and several earlier baselines omitted from the main table for brevity. The MLP, MLP with permutation augmentation, MLP with alignment, INR2Vec, Transformer, and DWS baselines are taken from the DWSNets evaluation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Navon et al., 2023</a>)</cite>; these results were originally reported on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST INR benchmarks. For methods evaluated on CIFAR-10 and augmented CIFAR-10, we additionally use the comparison reported by ScaleGMN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kalogeropoulos et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, which includes DWS, NFN, NG-GNN, ScaleGMN, and ScaleGMN-B on all four INR benchmarks. We further include results from Neural Graphs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kofinas et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, NFT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2023b</a>)</cite>, Monomial-NFN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tran et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, Quasi-Equivariant Monomial-NFN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tran et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, MAGEP-NFN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vo et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and ProbeGen <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kahana et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Results unavailable in the corresponding source are marked with “–”.</p>

<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Full Test-Accuracy Prediction Comparison</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ D.3 Full Test-Accuracy Prediction Comparison ‣ Appendix D Experimental details ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> provides an extended comparison on the neural-network test-accuracy prediction benchmarks. We include a broad range of approaches for learning from neural-network weights. MLP is a simple baseline operating directly on flattened network parameters, while StatNN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Unterthiner et al., 2020</a>)</cite> predicts performance from summary statistics of the weights and biases. SNE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Andreis et al., 2024</a>)</cite> represents neural networks using a hierarchical set-based encoder. We additionally include the permutation-equivariant NFN variants, NFN<sub id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_sub"><span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">NP</span></sub> and NFN<sub id="A4.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_sub"><span id="A4.SS3.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">HNP</span></sub> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2023a</a>)</cite>, as well as the scale- and permutation-aware ScaleGMN and ScaleGMN-B architectures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kalogeropoulos et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We further compare with graph-based weight-space models. NG-GNN and NG-T <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kofinas et al., 2024</a>)</cite> represent the input network as a graph and process it using a graph neural network or relational Transformer, respectively. DNG-Encoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al., 2026</a>)</cite> extends this approach by constructing a dynamic neural graph that models inference-time information flow. We also report the probe-enhanced Neural Graphs variants with 64 and 128 probes, as well as vanilla probing with 64 and 128 probes, following the evaluation of ProbeGen <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kahana et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Finally, we include NFT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al., 2023b</a>)</cite>, ProbeGen <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kahana et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and our HiddenProbe model. Results that were not reported for a particular benchmark are marked with “–”.</p>
</div>
