<section id="A4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.4 </span>Transformer Accuracy Prediction Across Thresholds</h3>

<div id="A4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following the evaluation protocol of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tran et al. (2026)</a></cite>, we additionally evaluate <span id="A4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> on subsets of networks obtained by applying accuracy thresholds of <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40\%</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>60</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>80</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80\%</annotation></semantics></math>. Tables <a href="#A4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ D.4 Transformer Accuracy Prediction Across Thresholds ‣ Appendix D Experimental details ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and <a href="#A4.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ D.4 Transformer Accuracy Prediction Across Thresholds ‣ Appendix D Experimental details ‣ Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> report the results for MNIST-Transformers and AGNews-Transformers, respectively. <span id="A4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span> consistently outperforms the previous state-of-the-art method, Transformer-NFN Quasi, achieving the highest Kendall’s <math id="A4.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> across all evaluated thresholds on both benchmarks.</p>
</div>

<td id="A4.T8.2.1.18.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="A4.T8.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.4</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A4.T8.2.1.18.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="A4.T8.m38" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.45" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.45</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.45</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A4.T8.2.1.18.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><math id="A4.T8.m39" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</span></div>

on three INR classification tasks, CIFAR-10-GS regression,
and MNIST-Transformers. INR and CNN counts are taken from

</section>

<section id="A4.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.7 </span>Tuning budget</h3>

<div id="A4.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For benchmarks on which ProbeGen had not previously been evaluated, we ran ProbeGen ourselves. We used the same hyper-parameter selection procedure for ProbeGen and for <span id="A4.SS7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>, ensuring that both methods were tuned under the same validation-based protocol. In all cases, we used the original benchmark train/validation/test splits and selected hyper-parameters using only the validation split.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For both methods, we fixed the batch size to <math id="A4.SS7.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>32</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math>, the number of learned probes to <math id="A4.SS7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>128</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">128</annotation></semantics></math>, and the weight decay to zero. All models were optimized with Adam.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For Transformer experiments, we used <math id="A4.SS7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>256</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">256</annotation></semantics></math> probes.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For each dataset, we performed a 27-configuration sweep over the learning rate and learning-rate scheduler. We considered learning rates</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="A4.Ex151" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex151.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{3\times 10^{-4},\,5\times 10^{-4},\,7\times 10^{-4}\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn> 7</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{3\times 10^{-4},\,5\times 10^{-4},\,7\times 10^{-4}\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For the ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler, we evaluated all combinations of</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<table id="A4.Ex152" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex152.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{patience}\in\{3,5\},\,\text{factor}\in\{0.2,0.3,0.5,0.7\}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>patience</mtext><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mtext>factor</mtext><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{patience}\in\{3,5\},\,\text{factor}\in\{0.2,0.3,0.5,0.7\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p8.1" class="ltx_p">for each learning rate, resulting in <math id="A4.SS7.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>24</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math> configurations. We additionally evaluated a cosine-annealing schedule for each of the three learning rates, yielding <math id="A4.SS7.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> further configurations and <math id="A4.SS7.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>27</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">27</annotation></semantics></math> configurations in total.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Each hyper-parameter configuration was first trained for <math id="A4.SS7.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math> epochs using seed <math id="A4.SS7.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>. For test-accuracy prediction, configurations were ranked exclusively according to validation Kendall’s <math id="A4.SS7.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>; test performance was not used for model selection. The best configuration for each method was then retrained using five seeds, <math id="A4.SS7.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0,\ldots,4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0,\ldots,4</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="A4.SS7.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="60" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>60</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math> epochs, and we report the mean and standard error of the resulting test Kendall’s <math id="A4.SS7.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS7.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS7.p10.1" class="ltx_p">For CIFAR-10 INR classification, we use the same 27-configuration optimization grid for both ProbeGen and <span id="A4.SS7.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">HiddenProbe</span>, but select the best configuration according to validation classification accuracy. The selected configuration is subsequently evaluated over five seeds. The final CIFAR-10 INR runs are trained for <math id="A4.SS7.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>30</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30</annotation></semantics></math> epochs.</p>
</div>
</section>
